GPU profiler and shadow draw counts agree on scope. | Removing casts changes ship relief and the station's depth. | Isolate station cast geometry and light ranges at 4K. |
| 6 | Post effects. Disabling SSAO, SSIL, glow and SSR together saved 0.480 ms GPU in scene 207 at 1080p. Godot showed 0.050 ms for SSAO, 0.080 ms for SSIL and 0.061 ms for glow in the profiled run. | 0.480 ms GPU for the combined switch. | Medium for the group. | Glow and contact shading affect readability. | Test each pass at the same render resolution and preserve the hit and shield looks. |
| 7 | Fog grid and dust. In the dense 4K storm, the 64×128 fog grid saved 0.140 ms GPU, full fog disable saved 0.249 ms and masking dust saved 0.120 ms. | Small. The grid change is the candidate that keeps the fog enabled. | Medium for GPU timing. | A smaller fog grid can soften detail or make steps visible. | Watch the bolt light moving across the gas at both cameras. |
| 8 | Battle and ship process callbacks. Diagnostic suspension lowered the main callback median by 1.675 ms for the battle or 0.971 ms for all 24 ship views in this sweep. Turning off the full effects engine lowered it by 2.158 ms. The profiler also found over 34,000 trail-mesh calls in the 720-frame gate sample. | The switches show scope for CPU work. A safe per-frame saving needs a narrower change. | Low for the switch deltas because the CPU pace varied. High for the observed call counts. | These controls also suspend world stepping, nameplates, ship motion or effects. | Replay identical motion and account for the time in damage and trail allocations. |
| 9 | Shield surface and hit routes. Fitted versus egg differed by 0.007 ms GPU at 1080p Max and 0.027 ms at 4K Max. Masking the shield draw and injecting extra hits or failures shifted the 1080p GPU median by less than 0.2 ms in the sweep. | The measured steady GPU differences are small. | High for the repeated shape baselines. Low for the short event switches. | Shield hit location and response are part of the chosen look. | Remeasure sustained clustered hits and close shots separately. |
| 10 | Particles, breakup and fragments. Masking the sprite and streak pools saved 0.057 ms GPU, and masking the impact-fragment pool saved 0.026 ms. The death control raised the 1080p GPU median by 0.333 ms. Hiding 13 breakup fragments during the same event schedule saved 0.016 ms GPU. | Little steady GPU time in these draw groups in scene 207. | Low for the event sweep. | Fragments carry breakup motion and silhouette. | Compare the cold event tails and the main-thread geometry work. |

Masking the storm-specific cards, volumes, lights and bolt meshes together saved 0.853 ms GPU in the dense 4K Max replay. Masking the eight bolt meshes alone moved the GPU median by 0.078 ms in the slower direction. Weather timing and compensation between passes can move a small reading by this amount.

Code inspection suggests more work on allocations. The fitted shield caches its triangle arrays and recreates the mesh and ray collider for a repeated hull type. The ship effects calculate a shield transform even when the shield surface is hidden. Moving trails build new vertex and index arrays and clear and refill their mesh surfaces. These are hypotheses for targeted CPU tests, with no gain included in the ranking. [Shield and trail code](../../../godot/fx/fx_ship.gd)

The original isolation pass logged light-indexing errors after teardown in five draw-mask cases. The affected timing results above use replays with draw layers and visibility restored before freeing the scene. The flat-material replay pauses volleys so live damage cannot replace the test materials mid-sample. [Isolation pass and replays](summary.json)

## Godot profiler

At 1080p Max, the station's depth pre-pass, opaque draw and light shadows took **1.230, 1.612 and 1.064 ms** on the GPU, compared with **0.478, 0.696 and 0.200 ms** in scene 207. The dense storm's transparent pass took **0.577 ms**, compared with **0.271 ms** in scene 207. These are medians of the GPU profiler's printed samples. [Raw profiler log](raw/profile_fitted_s1_engine.log.gz)

The per-hull test changed one hull's draw layers at a time and restored them afterward. All 24 scene 207 rows returned to the same draw totals. The Pyre-Barge `C19_51` removed 23 visible and 23 shadow draw submissions. The Sunward dreadnought `V1b_r_23` removed 22 and 22. The full inventory and per-hull submissions are in the profile trace. [Profile trace](raw/profile_fitted_s1.jsonl.gz)

In 720 profiled scene 207 frames, Godot recorded 17,304 nameplate updates, 34,608 trail-mesh calls, 36,330 hull-motion calls and 412 damage-material builds. The damage path includes background work to prepare breakup geometry and a main-thread pass to apply the new hull surfaces and materials. The script profiler adds overhead and includes worker and nested time. Its call counts and names identify the work, and the separate timing runs establish the wall-clock cost. [Profile trace](raw/profile_fitted_s1.jsonl.gz)

The fitted 1080p Max baseline held a median 6,764 live objects and 1,165 resources, with peaks of 8,072 objects and 1,196 resources. It submitted a median 481 visible draws and 318 shadow draws and used 2.45 GiB of video memory. These monitors track live use. Source inspection identifies the places that create fresh meshes, materials and arrays. [Monitor readings](summary.json)

## First-use timing

The cold probes start a fresh Godot process and keep the game's normal loading and warm-up. The natural storm watcher starts before the battle loads. Its first flare can occur under the loading cover. The other effects are triggered in order when the cover lifts, with their own sampling windows. Each frame trace keeps the viewport timing, main callback interval and FX section counters. A synchronous event dispatch can land between callback intervals, so the FX counters also identify time spent inside the trigger.

Scene 207, 1080p Max, three fresh starts per shape. Each cell gives the median and worst of the three peak frame times in ms. The breakup row covers the two frames on either side of the first wreck submission and the submission frame itself.

## Applied fix

Retain the alpha exterior shader in the battle's warm-up cache alongside the opaque exterior shader. The same shader code and uniforms serve the hull materials as before. Each of the six fitted Max baseline samples logged a late `exterior_alpha` creation. All six replay samples with the change reported zero late shader creations. The replay used the same scene 207 setup and both resolutions. [One-line fix](../../../godot/fx/fx.gd) [Trial data](summary.json)

| 4K | 11.493 / 39.990 / 644.465 ms | 11.448 / 26.506 / 61.044 ms | 5.835 / 5.819 ms |

The 1080p trial medians were 10.371, 14.206 and 10.387 ms. The median across launches passed the 12.5 ms gate and one session exceeded it. The late shader result verifies the reuse. The shorter observed worst frames and slower 1080p median came from different launch batches, so they give a range of observed behavior for the trial.

## Fixture and timing method

The benchmark uses main revision `be03488c5d03aabb0aec3480e949461c1c4f067e`, the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 with driver 617.42, the AMD Ryzen 7 5800X, and Godot 4.7.2 stable `ed1daf0bf` with Vulkan and Forward+. The installed ship manifest SHA-256 is `bb6258bc3f2a8c9e530776c4fd9a228957462beee10a37db73a37da0dc6ff2d1`. The generated asset manifest SHA-256 is `34244bddf5ae0b792bfd99d2313afba5a8beb319661346cfcdf81651652708c5`.

The live shared project still had the older egg default. The staging script copied its installed ship assets and generated cache to TEMP and layered the assigned revision's tracked Godot files over that copy. All 259 installed files matched their manifest entries. The placeholder guard stops on any missing hull.

| Fixture | Workload |
|---|---|
| Scene 207 | Seed 4207, standard scene-gate engagement camera, 20 hulls and four launch wings, HUD and seeded faction volleys. Fitted and egg use the same scene and presentation schedule. |
| Dense storm | PR 994 method, using seed 4103 and the actual terrain generator's nebula condition. 31 storm tiles, 28 nebula tiles, radius 170, live weather, HUD hidden and idle ships. |
| Sector 3 station | The game's `s4` encounter, seed 4004, ten Sunward Crusade hulls against ten Hegemony Navy hulls. Engagement camera, HUD and seeded presentation volleys. |

Timing starts after the load cover lifts, a 2.5 second activity settle, and 180 warm-up frames. Each sample takes at least 720 rendered frames and eight seconds. Every process takes the watchdog's solo GPU claim. The order of the cases and shield shapes reverses on session two. Vsync and the frame limiter are off. At 4K the renderer draws a 3840×2160 3D scene through 2× viewport scaling, the method used by scene 207 and PR 994. The window and HUD stay at 1920×1080. The full-detail storm and station runs establish the comparison for the geometry probes. The default baseline runs those two fixtures at the shipped LOD threshold and scene 207 at its full-detail gate setting. Raw headers record the project rendering settings and each row records the effective quality settings.

- **Frame** is elapsed wall-clock time between rendered frames.
- **Main CPU** covers the engine's process callbacks between an early and late callback on the main thread.
- **Render CPU** is Godot's measured viewport rendering CPU time. The project uses Godot's Safe thread model, so these are separate intervals of work even when they run on the same OS thread.
- **GPU** is Godot's viewport timer. Its readback can lag the main thread. These four measurements overlap and should be read independently.

Percentiles are calculated within each session. The tables take the median of the session medians, p95s and p99s, and the highest individual worst frame. A switch's saving compares its matched baseline at the same quality and resolution. Switch deltas can overlap. The changed-node count, draw counters, FX event markers and memory counters in the raw data show what each switch actually reached.

Use PowerShell 5.1 on the test PC, from the repo root. Choose a fresh output folder under TEMP. Staging takes the baseline from `HEAD`, including any files with edits in the checkout. The runs use the installed Godot 4.7.2 console build and the repo watchdog for every GPU launch. The watchdog waits for `gpu_go.txt` clearance and an empty GPU slot pool.

# R82: keep the ends violet even under a warm faction sky.
const NEBULA_FACTION_END_WEIGHT := 0.25
# The one scale table's terrain sizes (issue 710, R247; docs/playbooks/scale.md), world units, HEX_S = 10.
const GAS_PUFF_MIN := 24.0       # a nebula or storm puff's width
const GAS_PUFF_MAX := 34.0
const GAS_PUFF_REACH := 6.0      # how far a puff's centre sits off its hex centre
const GAS_VEIL_MIN := 36.0       # the faint high tying veil
const GAS_VEIL_MAX := 46.0
const GAS_MASK_MARGIN := 24.0    # the gas footprint reaches this far past its outermost hex centre
const DEBRIS_ROCK_MIN := 0.3     # a debris field's own rock, at scale 1 a library rock is 2 units long
const DEBRIS_ROCK_MAX := 2.8
# Issue 232 E17/NB5 sheet: the live weight, overridable for the three-weight capture (default is the shipped 0.25).
var faction_end_weight := clampf(float(OS.get_environment("VS_NEB_W")), 0.0, NEBULA_FACTION_END_WEIGHT) if OS.get_environment("VS_NEB_W") != "" else NEBULA_FACTION_END_WEIGHT

const GAS_SHADER := """
shader_type spatial;
render_mode unshaded, blend_mix, depth_draw_never, cull_disabled, shadows_disabled, fog_disabled;
""" + "%NOISE%" + """
uniform sampler2D depth_tex : hint_depth_texture, filter_nearest;
// r: the round field, g: inward feather of the union boundary, zero outside.
uniform sampler2D mask_tex : filter_linear, repeat_disable;
uniform vec4 mask_box = vec4(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0);
uniform vec3 c_dark = vec3(0.006, 0.002, 0.014);
uniform vec3 c_shadow = vec3(0.055, 0.012, 0.14);
uniform vec3 c_lit = vec3(0.43, 0.20, 0.80);
uniform vec3 c_glow = vec3(0.88, 0.72, 1.0);
uniform vec3 sun_v = vec3(0.45, 0.70, 0.55);
uniform float dens = 0.5;
uniform float gas_time = 0.0;
uniform float height_scale = 1.0;
uniform float glow_from = 0.56;
uniform float gain_a = 1.0;
uniform float flat_rates = 0.0;   // #230 NB8 capture variant (VS_GAS_FLAT=1): every layer at the base rate; 0 shipped
varying vec4 vI;
varying vec2 vQ;
varying vec3 vW;
void vertex() {
	vI = INSTANCE_CUSTOM; // x size, y spin, z density, floor(w) layer, fract(w) phase
	vec4 c = MODELVIEW_MATRIX * vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
	float a = vI.y * 6.2831;
	vec2 q = mat2(vec2(cos(a), sin(a)), vec2(-sin(a), cos(a))) * VERTEX.xy;
	vQ = VERTEX.xy * 2.0;
	c.xy += q * vI.x;
	vW = (INV_VIEW_MATRIX * c).xyz;
	POSITION = PROJECTION_MATRIX * c;
}
vec2 foot_at(vec2 xz) { return texture(mask_tex, (xz - mask_box.xy) * mask_box.zw).rg; }
void fragment() {
	float r = length(vQ);
	if (r > 1.0) { discard; }
	vec2 mask = foot_at(vW.xz);
	if (mask.g <= 0.001) { discard; }
	float dz = texture(depth_tex, SCREEN_UV).r;
	vec4 vv = INV_PROJECTION_MATRIX * vec4(SCREEN_UV * 2.0 - 1.0, dz, 1.0);
	vec3 opaque_world = (INV_VIEW_MATRIX * vec4(vv.xyz / vv.w, 1.0)).xyz;
	// All gas layers leave opaque hulls intact, even a veil in front of a ship.
	if (dz > 0.000001 && opaque_world.y > -20.0) { discard; }
	float band = floor(vI.w);
	float phase = fract(vI.w);
	// Layer rates and the base drift: contrib/opus/briefs/nebula_motion_spec.md (issue #230, NB8).
	float rate = band < 0.5 ? 0.6 : (band < 1.5 ? 1.0 : (band < 2.5 ? 1.6 : 0.4));
	if (flat_rates > 0.5) { rate = 1.0; }
	vec3 drift = vec3(0.012, 0.004, 0.007) * gas_time * rate;
	vec3 p = vW * 0.075 + drift;
	float w = wfbm3(p * 0.55 + 4.0);
	float n = wfbm3(p + vec3(w) * 0.9);
	vec2 wv = vec2(w - 0.5, wfbm3(p * 0.4 - 7.0) - 0.5) * 9.0;
	float fw = foot_at(vW.xz + wv).r;
	float breath = band > 0.5 && band < 1.5 ? sin(gas_time * 0.785398 + phase) * 0.025 : 0.0;
	float bar = 0.62 - 0.55 * smoothstep(0.3, 0.75, n);
	float foot = smoothstep(bar, bar + 0.3, fw) * mask.g;
	float lo = band < 0.5 ? -4.0 : (band < 1.5 ? 1.0 : (band < 2.5 ? 6.0 : 12.0));
	float hi = band < 0.5 ? 2.0 : (band < 1.5 ? 8.0 : (band < 2.5 ? 14.0 : 18.0));
	float layer = smoothstep(lo, lo + 1.5, vW.y / height_scale) * (1.0 - smoothstep(hi - 1.5, hi, vW.y / height_scale));
	float shape = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.4, 1.0, r);
	float field = smoothstep(0.27 + breath, 0.70 + breath, n);
	float d = shape * foot * layer * field * vI.z;
	// Soften contact with distant geometry below the playing surface.
	d *= clamp((-vv.z / vv.w + VERTEX.z) / 5.0, 0.0, 1.0);
	if (d <= 0.002) { discard; }
	float n2 = wfbm3(p + normalize(sun_v) * 0.22 + vec3(w) * 0.9);
	float lit = clamp(0.5 + (n - n2) * 5.0, 0.0, 1.0);
	float density = clamp((n - 0.18) / 0.72, 0.0, 1.0);
	vec3 col = mix(c_dark, c_shadow, smoothstep(0.0, 0.3, density));
	col = mix(col, c_lit, smoothstep(0.3, 0.6, density));
	col = mix(col, c_glow, smoothstep(0.6, 0.9, density));
	col *= 0.25 + 0.75 * lit;
	// R289: calm gas has broad soft radiance, never fine isocontours or electrical veins.
	vec3 energy = c_glow * smoothstep(0.67, 0.85, n) * 0.22;
	float layer_gain = band < 0.5 ? 0.50 : (band < 1.5 ? 1.0 : (band < 2.5 ? 0.55 : 0.10));
	// Optical depth accumulates across overlapping puffs rather than a flat tint.
	float a = 1.0 - exp(-d * dens * layer_gain * 3.6);
	float ship_band = 1.0 - smoothstep(3.0, 4.5, vW.y);
	a = min(a, mix(0.7, 0.39, ship_band));
	// Unshaded gas carries its internal light in the final radiance.
	ALBEDO = col + energy;
	ALPHA = clamp(a * gain_a, 0.0, 0.7);
}
"""

const BOLT_SHADER := """
shader_type spatial;
render_mode unshaded, blend_add, depth_draw_never, cull_disabled, shadows_disabled, fog_disabled;
const INFALL_SHADER := """
shader_type spatial;
render_mode unshaded, blend_mix, depth_draw_never, cull_disabled, shadows_disabled, fog_disabled;
uniform vec3 well = vec3(0.0);
uniform float r_out = 87.0;
varying vec2 vQ;
varying float fade;
void vertex() {
	float inner = 20.0;
	float cycle = r_out * 0.5 * log((3.0 * r_out - 2.0 * inner) / r_out);
	float phase = fract(TIME / cycle + INSTANCE_CUSTOM.y);
	float radius = r_out * 1.5 - r_out * 0.5 * exp(2.0 * phase * cycle / r_out);
	// dr/dt = -(3 - 2r/R); the tangential speed is one fifth of the inward speed.
	float angle = INSTANCE_CUSTOM.z * 6.2831853 + 0.2 * log(r_out / radius);
	vec3 p = well + vec3(cos(angle) * radius, 9.0 + INSTANCE_CUSTOM.w * 3.0, sin(angle) * radius);
	vec4 c = VIEW_MATRIX * vec4(p, 1.0);
	vQ = VERTEX.xy * 2.0;
	c.xy += VERTEX.xy * INSTANCE_CUSTOM.x;
	POSITION = PROJECTION_MATRIX * c;
	fade = smoothstep(0.0, 0.08, phase) * (1.0 - smoothstep(0.85, 1.0, phase));
}
void fragment() {
	float r = length(vQ);
	if (r > 1.0) { discard; }
	ALBEDO = vec3(0.32, 0.17, 0.12);
	ALPHA = 0.15 * fade * exp(-r * r * 4.0);
}
"""


func build(world) -> void:
	W = world
	# battle.gd _play_event("tick") calls _float("Ion storm") before gfx.tick.
	# Consume those positioned presentation records, never the rules event queue.
	var presenter: Node = W.get_parent()
	if presenter != null and presenter.get("floats") is Array:
		_tick_presenter = presenter
	rng.seed = int(W.setting.get("seed", 7)) * 31 + 991
	var pts: Dictionary = W._terr_pts
	# Background specks originally drew after gas at priority 0. Put them behind it.
	for child in W.get_children():
		if child is MultiMeshInstance3D and child.material_override is ShaderMaterial:
			var mat: ShaderMaterial = child.material_override
			if mat.shader.code == W.DUST_SHADER:
				mat.render_priority = -6
	for kind in ["neb", "storm"]:
		var patches := _patches(pts[kind])
		var broad_left := (pts[kind] as Array).size() / 3
		for j in patches.size():
			var broad := (patches[j] as Array).size() / 3 if j < patches.size() - 1 else broad_left
			_gas(patches[j], kind == "storm", broad)
			broad_left -= broad
	if not (pts["storm"] as Array).is_empty():
		_bolts(pts["storm"])
	if not (pts["debris"] as Array).is_empty():
		_debris(pts["debris"])
	if W._well != Vector3.INF:
		_well(W._well)


func set_gas_k(k: float) -> void:
	for g in gas_mats:
		(g[0] as ShaderMaterial).set_shader_parameter("gain_a", float(g[1]) * k)
	for m in fog_mats:
		m.set_shader_parameter("gain_a", k)


func _quad_mm(n: int) -> MultiMesh:
	var mm := MultiMesh.new()
	mm.transform_format = MultiMesh.TRANSFORM_3D
	mm.use_custom_data = true
	var qm := QuadMesh.new()
	qm.size = Vector2(1, 1)
	mm.mesh = qm
	mm.instance_count = n
	return mm


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- nebula and storm gas

# Connected components keep broad veils and materials local to each cloud.
func _patches(ps: Array) -> Array:
	var remaining := ps.duplicate()
	var patches: Array = []
	while not remaining.is_empty():
		var patch: Array = [remaining.pop_back()]
		var i := 0
		while i < patch.size():
			for j in range(remaining.size() - 1, -1, -1):
				if (patch[i] as Vector3).distance_squared_to(remaining[j]) < 18.0 * 18.0:
					patch.append(remaining[j])
					remaining.remove_at(j)
			i += 1
		patches.append(patch)
	return patches


static func _gas_card_shader(storm: bool) -> String:
	# Expanded cards cover much more than their thin height bands. Reject empty
	# support before the expensive noise, using the accepted shader's own math.
	# Hoist its declarations rather than keeping another table of layer sizes.
	var code: String = ION.CARDS if storm else GAS_SHADER
	var declarations := ["float lo =", "float hi =", "float y =", "float layer =", "float shape ="]
	if storm:
		declarations.append("float foot =")
	var support := PackedStringArray()
	var body := PackedStringArray()
	var in_fragment := false
	for line in code.split("\n"):
		if line == "void fragment() {":
			in_fragment = true
		var move := false
		if in_fragment:
			for declaration in declarations:
				if line.strip_edges().begins_with(declaration):
					move = true
					break
		if move:
			support.append(line)
		else:
			body.append(line)
	var anchor := "\tfloat band = floor(%s.w);" % ("cloud" if storm else "vI")
	# Remaining field and contact factors are in [0, 1]. Zero support already
	# produced zero density and was discarded; no visible samples are removed.
	var bound := "shape * cloud.z" if storm else "shape * mask.g * layer * vI.z"
	var early := "\n".join(support) + "\n\tif (" + bound + " <= 0.0) { discard; }"
	return "\n".join(body).replace(anchor, anchor + "\n" + early).replace("%NOISE%", WS.NOISE)


func _gas(ps: Array, storm: bool, broad_count := -1) -> void:
	var low: bool = W.quality == "low"
	var expanded := gas_route != "today"
	var volume: bool = gas_route == "fog" and W.quality == "max"
	# step 2: fewer, broader, softer puffs; their shape comes from one noise field and the patch's footprint (_mask), so
	# the patch reads as one body of gas, not a row of cotton balls on hex tiles
	var per := 3 if low else 5
	if expanded:
		per = 2 if volume or low else 5
	var n_big := ps.size() / 3 if broad_count < 0 else broad_count
	var mm := _quad_mm(ps.size() * per + n_big)
	var i := 0
	for p in ps:
		for k in per:
			var a := rng.randf() * TAU
			var rr := sqrt(rng.randf()) * GAS_PUFF_REACH
			# Preserve the count and size; split the existing puffs into height bands.
			var layer: int = [0, 1, 2, 1, 2][k % 5]
			# Low drops the dim bottom puff, retaining the core and upper layer.
			if expanded and low:
				layer = k + 1
			var y := rng.randf_range(-2.5, 0.5) if layer == 0 else (rng.randf_range(2.5, 6.5) if layer == 1 else rng.randf_range(8.0, 12.0))
			if expanded:
				y *= GAS_HEIGHT
			mm.set_instance_transform(i, Transform3D(Basis.IDENTITY, (p as Vector3) + Vector3(cos(a) * rr, y, sin(a) * rr)))
			mm.set_instance_custom_data(i, Color(rng.randf_range(GAS_PUFF_MIN, GAS_PUFF_MAX), rng.randf(), rng.randf_range(0.55, 0.85), layer + rng.randf() * 0.9))
			if expanded:
				var cd := mm.get_instance_custom_data(i)
				cd.r *= GAS_CLOUD_SCALE
				cd.b *= 0.55 if volume else 1.0
				mm.set_instance_custom_data(i, cd)
			i += 1
	# One or two existing broad puffs become a very faint high tying veil.
	for k in n_big:
		var p: Vector3 = ps[rng.randi() % ps.size()]
		mm.set_instance_transform(i, Transform3D(Basis.IDENTITY, p + Vector3(rng.randf_range(-4, 4), rng.randf_range(13.5, 16.5) if k < 2 else rng.randf_range(2.5, 6.5), rng.randf_range(-4, 4))))
		mm.set_instance_custom_data(i, Color(rng.randf_range(GAS_VEIL_MIN, GAS_VEIL_MAX), rng.randf(), rng.randf_range(0.3, 0.4), (3 if k < 2 else 1) + rng.randf() * 0.9))
		if expanded:
			var transform := mm.get_instance_transform(i)
			transform.origin.y *= GAS_HEIGHT
			mm.set_instance_transform(i, transform)
			var custom := mm.get_instance_custom_data(i)
			custom.r *= GAS_CLOUD_SCALE
			custom.b *= 0.55 if volume else 1.0
			mm.set_instance_custom_data(i, custom)
		i += 1
	var mi := MultiMeshInstance3D.new()
	mi.name = "Storm" if storm else "Nebula"
	mi.multimesh = mm
	var m := ShaderMaterial.new()
	var sh := Shader.new()
	sh.code = _gas_card_shader(storm)
	m.shader = sh
	if expanded:
		m.set_shader_parameter("height_scale", GAS_HEIGHT)
	m.set_shader_parameter("sun_v", Vector3(0.45, 0.70, 0.55))   # world.gd SUN
	if OS.get_environment("VS_GAS_FLAT") == "1":
		m.set_shader_parameter("flat_rates", 1.0)   # capture variant only (#230 NB8); never set in play
	var mk: Array = _mask(ps, 1.5 if storm else 2.0)
	m.set_shader_parameter("mask_tex", mk[0])
	m.set_shader_parameter("mask_box", mk[1])
	var g := 1.0
	if storm:
		# R282: the cloud carries broad cool charge, not the old warm contour veins.
		storm_mats.append(m)
		_storm_patches.append({"mat": m, "points": ps, "tick": 0.0})
		_set_flashes([])
	else:
		var b: Array = FLOOK.of(W._fac).get("nebula", FLOOK.of("voidsworn")["nebula"])
		var violet := Vector3(0.434, 0.202, 1.0) # legend #b07cff in linear RGB
		var faction: Vector3 = b[1]
		# Match value before the hue blend, so warm skies cannot make brown gas.
		faction /= maxf(faction.length(), 0.001)
		var end_tint := faction
		m.set_shader_parameter("c_dark", Vector3(0.006, 0.002, 0.014).lerp(end_tint * Vector3(0.006, 0.002, 0.014).length(), faction_end_weight))
		m.set_shader_parameter("c_shadow", Vector3(0.055, 0.012, 0.14))
		var body := violet.lerp(faction * violet.length(), 0.5)
		# R82 fixes the violet family: a warm sky may shift it, never neutralise it.
		body.y = minf(body.y, body.z * 0.24)
		body.x = minf(body.x, body.z * 0.60)
		m.set_shader_parameter("c_lit", body * 0.65)
		m.set_shader_parameter("c_glow", Vector3(0.88, 0.72, 1.0).lerp(end_tint * Vector3(0.88, 0.72, 1.0).length(), faction_end_weight))
		m.set_shader_parameter("dens", 0.5)
	# drawn before the board's own fills, so a move hex inside the gas still shows on top
	m.render_priority = -5
	gas_mats.append([m, g])
	mi.material_override = m
	mi.cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF
	# Vertex-expanded cards need bounds that include their scaled visible radius.

func _event(event: String, index: int) -> String:
	var fx = b.gfx
	var ids: Array = side_ids.player
	var id: String = ids[index % ids.size()]
	var ship = fx.ship(id)
	match event:
		"shield_hit":
			var aim: Vector3 = ship.to_world(ship.hull.shield_centre() + Vector3(0, 20, 0))
			var contact: Dictionary = ship.shield_point(aim)
			ship.shield_hit(fx, contact.local, fx.now, 1.0, 3.0)
		"shield_failure":
			fx.shield_break(id, 0)
		"death":
			fx.death(id, "big")
			ids.erase(id)
		"fragment_burst":
			var attacker: String = side_ids.enemy[0]
			fx.volley(attacker, "battery", id, {"weapon_id": LOOKS[fac_of[attacker]][0][1],
				"shots": [true, true, true], "hits": [{"hull": 40, "section": "mid"}, {"hull": 40, "section": "mid"}, {"hull": 40, "section": "mid"}]})
	return id


func _watch_storm() -> void:
	var now := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	var previous := storm_frame
	storm_frame = now
	if b == null or not is_instance_valid(b.world) or not is_instance_valid(b.world._living) or previous == 0:
		return
	var living = b.world._living
	var frames: Array = storm_trace.samples
	if int(storm_trace.started) == 0:
		for bolt in living.bolts:
			if float(bolt.start) >= 0 and living.clock > float(bolt.start):
				storm_trace.started = now
				storm_trace.pre_frames = frames.size()
				storm_trace.loading = b.warming
				storm_trace.storm_clock = living.clock
				storm_trace.pipe_before = _pipes()
				break
	if int(storm_trace.started) > 0 and now - int(storm_trace.started) >= 650000:
		return
	frames.append(_sample(get_viewport().get_viewport_rid(), now - previous))
	if int(storm_trace.started) == 0 and frames.size() > 16:
		frames.pop_front()
	if int(storm_trace.started) > 0:
		storm_trace.pipe_after = _pipes()

# Issue 368, R289. Steel-blue and cyan weather, distinct from calm purple nebula gas.
# Both tiers sample volumes in world space. Charge gathers in broad cloud lobes,
# never in persistent contour lines. Only the intermittent fork meshes draw arcs.
const CARDS := """
shader_type spatial;
render_mode unshaded, blend_mix, depth_draw_never, cull_disabled, shadows_disabled, fog_disabled;
%NOISE%
uniform sampler2D depth_tex : hint_depth_texture, filter_nearest;
uniform sampler2D mask_tex : filter_linear, repeat_disable;
uniform vec4 mask_box;
uniform float gas_time = 0.0;
uniform float height_scale = 1.0;
uniform float gain_a = 1.0;
uniform vec4 flashes[8];
uniform vec4 tick_flare = vec4(0.0);
varying vec4 cloud;
varying vec2 disc;
varying vec3 world;
void vertex() {
	cloud = INSTANCE_CUSTOM;
	vec4 c = MODELVIEW_MATRIX * vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
	float a = cloud.y * 6.2831;
	vec2 q = mat2(vec2(cos(a), sin(a)), vec2(-sin(a), cos(a))) * VERTEX.xy;
	disc = VERTEX.xy * 2.0;
	c.xy += q * cloud.x;
	world = (INV_VIEW_MATRIX * c).xyz;
	POSITION = PROJECTION_MATRIX * c;
}
void fragment() {
	float radius = length(disc);
	if (radius > 1.0) { discard; }
	vec2 uv = (world.xz - mask_box.xy) * mask_box.zw;
	if (any(lessThan(uv, vec2(0.0))) || any(greaterThan(uv, vec2(1.0)))) { discard; }
	vec2 mask = texture(mask_tex, uv).rg;
	float depth = texture(depth_tex, SCREEN_UV).r;
	vec4 view_pos = INV_PROJECTION_MATRIX * vec4(SCREEN_UV * 2.0 - 1.0, depth, 1.0);
	vec3 opaque = (INV_VIEW_MATRIX * vec4(view_pos.xyz / view_pos.w, 1.0)).xyz;
	if (depth > 0.000001 && opaque.y > -20.0) { discard; }
	float band = floor(cloud.w);
	float rate = band < 0.5 ? 0.6 : (band < 1.5 ? 1.0 : (band < 2.5 ? 1.6 : -0.4));
	vec3 p = world * vec3(0.055, 0.075, 0.055) + vec3(0.027, 0.009, 0.015) * gas_time * rate;
	float warp = wfbm3(p * 0.5 + 4.0);
	float n = wfbm3(p + vec3(warp * 0.8));
	float detail = wfbm3(p * 2.3 + vec3(3.7, 1.2, 7.4));
	float foot = mask.g * smoothstep(0.08, 0.55, mask.r);
	float lo = band < 0.5 ? -4.0 : (band < 1.5 ? 1.0 : (band < 2.5 ? 6.0 : 12.0));
	float hi = band < 0.5 ? 2.0 : (band < 1.5 ? 8.0 : (band < 2.5 ? 14.0 : 18.0));
	float y = world.y / height_scale;
	float layer = smoothstep(lo, lo + 1.5, y) * (1.0 - smoothstep(hi - 1.5, hi, y));
	float field = smoothstep(0.38, 0.74, n);
	float shape = (1.0 - smoothstep(0.25, 1.0, radius)) * foot * layer;
	float density = shape * field * cloud.z;
	density *= clamp((-view_pos.z / view_pos.w + VERTEX.z) / 5.0, 0.0, 1.0);
	if (density < 0.002) { discard; }
	float sun = wfbm3(p + vec3(warp * 0.8) + vec3(0.12, 0.20, 0.15));
	float rim = clamp(0.45 + (n - sun) * 5.0, 0.0, 1.0);
	float charge = smoothstep(0.47, 0.70, detail) * smoothstep(0.38, 0.65, n);
	vec3 col = mix(vec3(0.006, 0.014, 0.022), vec3(0.032, 0.065, 0.11), field);
	col += vec3(0.04, 0.13, 0.18) * rim * field;
	col += vec3(0.10, 0.42, 0.52) * charge * (0.35 + 0.04 * sin(gas_time * 2.8 + cloud.y * 6.28));
	float flash = tick_flare.w * 0.12;
	for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
		vec3 delta = world - flashes[i].xyz;
		flash += exp(-dot(delta, delta) / 240.0) * flashes[i].w;
	}
	col += vec3(0.14, 0.55, 1.05) * flash * field * 1.2;
	float weight = band < 0.5 ? 0.50 : (band < 1.5 ? 1.0 : (band < 2.5 ? 0.65 : 0.16));
	ALBEDO = col;
	ALPHA = min(0.58, (1.0 - exp(-density * weight * 2.5)) * gain_a);
}

func _build_shield(fx) -> void:
	var sph = SphereMesh.new()
	sph.radius = 1.0
	sph.height = 2.0
	sph.radial_segments = 64
	sph.rings = 32
	# Ryan, Nov 18 (issue 1045): the fitted skin replaces the R297 egg default.
	# Select the egg with rendering/effects/shield_shape="egg" or VS_SHIELD_SHAPE=egg.
	var shape := OS.get_environment("VS_SHIELD_SHAPE")
	if shape.is_empty():
		shape = str(ProjectSettings.get_setting("rendering/effects/shield_shape", "fitted"))
	var skin: Mesh = _shield_skin() if shape == "fitted" else sph
	if skin == null:
		skin = sph
	_shield_mat = fx.mat(SH.SHIELD, 2)
	_shield_mat.set_shader_parameter("fitted_shape", _shield_tm != null)
	var sc: Color = fac["shield"]
	_shield_mat.set_shader_parameter("col", Vector3(sc.r, sc.g, sc.b) * 2.2)
	_shield_mat.set_shader_parameter("rad", hull.shield_radii())
	_shield_mat.set_shader_parameter("style", int(fac["shield_style"]))
	var se = fac.get("shield_edge")
	if se is Color:
		_shield_mat.set_shader_parameter("edge_mode", 1)
		_shield_mat.set_shader_parameter("edge_col", Vector3(se.r, se.g, se.b))
	elif se is String and se == "rainbow":
		_shield_mat.set_shader_parameter("edge_mode", 2)
	var hits = PackedVector4Array()
	var hw = PackedVector4Array()
	for i in 6:
		hits.append(Vector4(0, 0, 0, -100))
		hw.append(Vector4(0, 1, 1, 0))
	_hits = hits
	_hitw = hw
	_shield_mat.set_shader_parameter("hits", hits)
	_shield_mat.set_shader_parameter("hitw", hw)
	_shield_mi = MeshInstance3D.new()
	_shield_mi.name = "fx_shield"
	_shield_mi.mesh = skin
	_shield_mi.material_override = _shield_mat
	_shield_mi.position = hull.shield_centre()
	_shield_mi.scale = Vector3.ONE if _shield_tm != null else hull.shield_radii()
	_shield_pose = _shield_mi.transform
	_shield_mi.cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF
	_shield_mi.visible = false
	root.add_child(_shield_mi)


func _shield_skin() -> ArrayMesh:
	var frames := {}
	var box := AABB()
	var view := root as SHIP_VIEW
	var visual: Node3D = view.hull if view != null else null
	var bob := visual.position - view.hull_base if visual != null else Vector3.ZERO
	for m in meshes:
		var mi := m as MeshInstance3D
		if mi == null or mi.mesh == null:
			continue
		# Compose local transforms to avoid roundoff from world position and facing.
		var frame := Transform3D.IDENTITY
		var part: Node3D = mi
		while part != root and part != null and not part.top_level:
			var local := part.transform
			if part == visual:
				local.origin = view.hull_base
			frame = local * frame
			part = part.get_parent_node_3d()
		if part != root:
			frame = root.global_transform.affine_inverse() * mi.global_transform
		var bounds: AABB = frame * mi.mesh.get_aabb()
		box = bounds if frames.is_empty() else box.merge(bounds)
		frames[mi] = frame
	var faces := HULL.faces_of(root, meshes, null, frames)
	if faces.is_empty():
		return null
	var digest := HashingContext.new()
	digest.start(HashingContext.HASH_SHA256)
	digest.update(var_to_bytes(box))
	digest.update(faces.to_byte_array())
	var key := digest.finish().hex_encode()
	if not _shield_skin_arrays.has(key):
		var arrays := _bake_shield_skin(box, faces)
		if arrays.is_empty():
			return null
		if _shield_skin_arrays.size() >= SHIELD_SKIN_CACHE_LIMIT:
			_shield_skin_arrays.erase(_shield_skin_arrays.keys()[0])
		_shield_skin_arrays[key] = arrays
	# The cache is in the unbobbed frame. Hits and the shader use coordinates
	# relative to the active core, just as they do for the egg.
	var posed: Array = _shield_skin_arrays[key].duplicate()
	posed[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] = Transform3D(Basis.IDENTITY, bob - hull.shield_centre()) * (posed[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] as PackedVector3Array)
	var skin := ArrayMesh.new()
	skin.add_surface_from_arrays(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES, posed)
	_shield_tm = TriangleMesh.new()
	_shield_tm.create_from_faces(skin.get_faces())
	return skin


func _bake_shield_skin(box: AABB, faces: PackedVector3Array) -> Array:
	# R303: offset sampled hull surfaces, rather than stretching a sphere from the
	# core. Uniform cells along the whole hull preserve waists and open ring holes.
	# Only the outside of the offset volume is meshed, never interior armour skins.
	var surface := TriangleMesh.new()
	if not surface.create_from_faces(faces):
		return []
	var length := maxf(box.size.x, 0.1)
	var cross_span := maxf(minf(box.size.y, box.size.z), 0.05)
	var step := maxf(length / 128.0, minf(length / 96.0, cross_span / 12.0))
	var gap := maxf(cross_span * 0.08, step * 1.5)
	var margin := gap + step * 3.0
	var origin := box.position - Vector3.ONE * margin
	var size := Vector3i((box.size + Vector3.ONE * margin * 2.0) / step) + Vector3i.ONE * 2
	var stride := Vector3i(1, size.x, size.x * size.y)
	var field := PackedFloat32Array()
	field.resize(size.x * size.y * size.z)
	field.fill(pow(gap / step + 2.0, 2.0))
	var sampled := PackedByteArray()
	sampled.resize(field.size())
	# Each sweep visits every intersection, including the inside edge of a ring.
	# The three axes also sample faces edge-on to either of the other two sweeps.
	for axis in 3:
		var u := (axis + 1) % 3
		var v := (axis + 2) % 3
		var direction := Vector3.ZERO
		direction[axis] = 1.0
		for a in size[u]:
			for b in size[v]:
				var start := origin
				start[u] += a * step
				start[v] += b * step
				for crossing in 128:
					var hit := surface.intersect_ray(start, direction)
					if hit.is_empty(): break
					var at: Vector3 = hit["position"]
					var p := (at - origin) / step
					var cell := Vector3i(p).clamp(Vector3i.ZERO, size - Vector3i.ONE)
					var sample_i := cell.x + cell.y * stride.y + cell.z * stride.z
					if sampled[sample_i] == 0:
						sampled[sample_i] = 1
						_shield_sample(field, size, stride, p, gap / step + 1.5)
					start = at + direction * step * 0.04
	# Signed distance to the sampled surface. Flood from empty space, filling only
	# sealed cavities. A ring's through-hole remains connected to outside space.
	var threshold := (gap / step) * (gap / step)
	for i in field.size():
		var value := field[i] - threshold
		# Keep crossings away from exact grid corners, where float rounding can
		# collapse distinct edge vertices into zero-area triangles.
		field[i] = value if absf(value) > 0.001 else (0.001 if value >= 0.0 else -0.001)
	var outside := PackedByteArray()
	outside.resize(field.size())
	var queue := PackedInt32Array([0])
	outside[0] = 1
	var head := 0
	while head < queue.size():
		var i := queue[head]
		head += 1
		var cell := Vector3i(i % size.x, (i / size.x) % size.y, i / stride.z)
		for axis in 3:
			for sign_i in [-1, 1]:
				if cell[axis] + sign_i < 0 or cell[axis] + sign_i >= size[axis]: continue
				var j: int = i + stride[axis] * sign_i
				if outside[j] == 0 and field[j] > 0.0:
					outside[j] = 1
					queue.append(j)
	for i in field.size():

	var view := root as SHIP_VIEW
	var visual: Node3D = view.hull if view != null else null
	var bob := visual.position - view.hull_base if visual != null else Vector3.ZERO
	for m in meshes:
		var mi := m as MeshInstance3D
		if mi == null or mi.mesh == null:
			continue
		# Compose local transforms to avoid roundoff from world position and facing.
		var frame := Transform3D.IDENTITY
		var part: Node3D = mi
		while part != root and part != null and not part.top_level:
			var local := part.transform
			if part == visual:
				local.origin = view.hull_base
			frame = local * frame
			part = part.get_parent_node_3d()
		if part != root:
			frame = root.global_transform.affine_inverse() * mi.global_transform
		var bounds: AABB = frame * mi.mesh.get_aabb()
		box = bounds if frames.is_empty() else box.merge(bounds)
		frames[mi] = frame
	var faces := HULL.faces_of(root, meshes, null, frames)
	if faces.is_empty():
		return null
	var digest := HashingContext.new()
	digest.start(HashingContext.HASH_SHA256)
	digest.update(var_to_bytes(box))
	digest.update(faces.to_byte_array())
	var key := digest.finish().hex_encode()
	if not _shield_skin_arrays.has(key):
		var arrays := _bake_shield_skin(box, faces)
		if arrays.is_empty():
			return null
		if _shield_skin_arrays.size() >= SHIELD_SKIN_CACHE_LIMIT:
			_shield_skin_arrays.erase(_shield_skin_arrays.keys()[0])
		_shield_skin_arrays[key] = arrays
	# The cache is in the unbobbed frame. Hits and the shader use coordinates
	# relative to the active core, just as they do for the egg.
	var posed: Array = _shield_skin_arrays[key].duplicate()
	posed[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] = Transform3D(Basis.IDENTITY, bob - hull.shield_centre()) * (posed[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] as PackedVector3Array)
	var skin := ArrayMesh.new()
	skin.add_surface_from_arrays(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES, posed)
	_shield_tm = TriangleMesh.new()
	_shield_tm.create_from_faces(skin.get_faces())
	return skin


func _bake_shield_skin(box: AABB, faces: PackedVector3Array) -> Array:
	# R303: offset sampled hull surfaces, rather than stretching a sphere from the
	# core. Uniform cells along the whole hull preserve waists and open ring holes.
	# Only the outside of the offset volume is meshed, never interior armour skins.
	var surface := TriangleMesh.new()
	if not surface.create_from_faces(faces):
		return []
	var length := maxf(box.size.x, 0.1)
	var cross_span := maxf(minf(box.size.y, box.size.z), 0.05)
	var step := maxf(length / 128.0, minf(length / 96.0, cross_span / 12.0))
	var gap := maxf(cross_span * 0.08, step * 1.5)
	var margin := gap + step * 3.0
	var origin := box.position - Vector3.ONE * margin
	var size := Vector3i((box.size + Vector3.ONE * margin * 2.0) / step) + Vector3i.ONE * 2
	var stride := Vector3i(1, size.x, size.x * size.y)
	var field := PackedFloat32Array()
	field.resize(size.x * size.y * size.z)
	field.fill(pow(gap / step + 2.0, 2.0))
	var sampled := PackedByteArray()
	sampled.resize(field.size())
	# Each sweep visits every intersection, including the inside edge of a ring.
	# The three axes also sample faces edge-on to either of the other two sweeps.
	for axis in 3:
		var u := (axis + 1) % 3
		var v := (axis + 2) % 3
		var direction := Vector3.ZERO
		direction[axis] = 1.0
		for a in size[u]:
			for b in size[v]:
				var start := origin
				start[u] += a * step
				start[v] += b * step
				for crossing in 128:
					var hit := surface.intersect_ray(start, direction)
					if hit.is_empty(): break
					var at: Vector3 = hit["position"]
					var p := (at - origin) / step
					var cell := Vector3i(p).clamp(Vector3i.ZERO, size - Vector3i.ONE)
					var sample_i := cell.x + cell.y * stride.y + cell.z * stride.z
					if sampled[sample_i] == 0:
						sampled[sample_i] = 1
						_shield_sample(field, size, stride, p, gap / step + 1.5)
					start = at + direction * step * 0.04
	# Signed distance to the sampled surface. Flood from empty space, filling only
	# sealed cavities. A ring's through-hole remains connected to outside space.
	var threshold := (gap / step) * (gap / step)
	for i in field.size():
		var value := field[i] - threshold
		# Keep crossings away from exact grid corners, where float rounding can
		# collapse distinct edge vertices into zero-area triangles.
		field[i] = value if absf(value) > 0.001 else (0.001 if value >= 0.0 else -0.001)
	var outside := PackedByteArray()
	outside.resize(field.size())
	var queue := PackedInt32Array([0])
	outside[0] = 1
	var head := 0
	while head < queue.size():
		var i := queue[head]
		head += 1
		var cell := Vector3i(i % size.x, (i / size.x) % size.y, i / stride.z)
		for axis in 3:
			for sign_i in [-1, 1]:
				if cell[axis] + sign_i < 0 or cell[axis] + sign_i >= size[axis]: continue
				var j: int = i + stride[axis] * sign_i
				if outside[j] == 0 and field[j] > 0.0:
					outside[j] = 1
					queue.append(j)
"""Keep full frame traces and derive JSON tables without pooling the sessions."""

import argparse
import gzip
import hashlib
import json
import math
import statistics
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path


def summarize(samples, columns):
    if not samples or any(len(frame) != len(columns) for frame in samples):
        raise ValueError("Missing or malformed frame samples")
    stats = {}
    for key, values in zip(columns, zip(*samples)):
        ordered = sorted(values)
        stats[key] = {
            "median": round(statistics.median(ordered), 3),
            "p95": round(ordered[math.ceil(0.95 * len(ordered)) - 1], 3),
            "p99": round(ordered[math.ceil(0.99 * len(ordered)) - 1], 3),
            "max": round(ordered[-1], 3),
        }
    return stats


def write_json(path, data):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def write_baseline(path, groups):
    names = {"gate": "Scene 207", "dense": "Dense storm", "large": "Sector 3 station"}
    metrics = ("frame_ms", "main_process_ms", "render_cpu_ms", "gpu_ms")
    lines = [
        "# Baseline timing",
        "",
        "Each timing cell is median / p95 / p99 / worst in ms. "
        "See the [method and fixture details](README.md).",
        "",
        "| Fixture | Shield | Quality | 3D | Mesh LOD | Sessions | Frame | Main CPU | Render CPU | GPU |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|",
    ]
    baseline = [row for row in groups if row["phase"].startswith("baseline")]
    for row in sorted(baseline, key=lambda row: (
        list(names).index(row["case"].split(":")[0]),
        row["shield"] != "fitted",
        ["max", "high", "low"].index(row["case"].split(":")[1]),
        row["case"].split(":")[2],
        row["case"].split(":")[3] != "native_lod",
    )):
        fixture, tier, scale, variant = row["case"].split(":")
        cells = [names[fixture], row["shield"], tier, "1080p" if scale == "1" else "4K",
                 "Shipped" if variant == "native_lod" else "Full detail", str(row["sessions"])]
        cells.extend(" / ".join(f"{row['stats'][metric][stat]:.3f}" for stat in ("median", "p95", "p99", "max"))
                     for metric in metrics)
        lines.append("| " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("work", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("out", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    result = {"machine": json.loads((args.work / "machine.json").read_text())}
    raw = args.out / "raw"
    raw.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    runs = []
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    gate = []
    rejected = []
    probes = {}
    for path in sorted((args.work / "run").glob("*/*/samples.jsonl")):
        phase, process, _ = path.relative_to(args.work / "run").parts
        records = [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()]
        if not records:
            rejected.append({"phase": phase, "process": process, "reason": "Empty sample journal"})
            continue
        info, *rows = records
        if not rows:
            rejected.append({"phase": phase, "process": process, "reason": "No completed case"})
            continue
        if not info["adapter"] or info["renderer"] != "forward_plus":
            raise ValueError(f"{path} has no windowed Forward+ run")
        for manifest in ("ship", "gen"):
            if info[f"{manifest}_manifest_sha256"] != result["machine"][f"installed_{manifest}_manifest_sha256"]:
                raise ValueError(f"Manifest changed during {path}")
        trace = raw / f"{phase}_{process}.jsonl.gz"
        trace.write_bytes(gzip.compress(path.read_bytes(), mtime=0))
        record = {"phase": phase, "process": process, "trace": trace.name, "rows": []}
        probe = path.parents[1] / "probe.gd"
        if phase not in probes and probe.exists():
            source = probe.read_bytes()
            if hashlib.sha256(source).hexdigest() != info["source_sha256"]:
                raise ValueError(f"Probe hash does not match {phase} trace")
            stored = raw / f"{phase}_probe.gd.gz"
            stored.write_bytes(gzip.compress(source, mtime=0))
            probes[phase] = stored.name
        if phase in probes:
            record["probe"] = probes[phase]
        telemetry = path.with_name("gpu.csv")
        if telemetry.exists():
            record["gpu_before_after_csv"] = telemetry.read_text(encoding="ascii").splitlines()
        engine_log = path.with_name("engine.log")
        if engine_log.exists():
            errors = Counter(line for line in engine_log.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
                             if line.startswith(("ERROR:", "SCRIPT ERROR:")))
            if errors:
                record["godot_errors"] = errors
        runs.append(record)
        if phase == "profile":
            profiler = raw / f"{phase}_{process}_engine.log.gz"
            profiler.write_bytes(gzip.compress(engine_log.read_bytes(), mtime=0))
            record["profiler"] = profiler.name
        for row in rows:
            samples = row.pop("samples", None)
            if samples is not None:
                row["sample_count"] = len(samples)
                row["stats"] = summarize(samples, info["metrics"])
                fx_trace = row.pop("fx_profile_by_frame_us", [])
                if fx_trace:
                    spikes = sorted(range(len(samples)), key=lambda index: samples[index][0], reverse=True)[:5]
                    row["worst_five_fx_us"] = [[index, samples[index][:4], fx_trace[index]] for index in spikes]
                if row["stats"]["gpu_ms"]["median"] <= 0:
                    raise ValueError(f"No GPU timings for {phase} {process} {row['case']}")
                if phase != "profile":
                    groups[(phase, info["shield"], row["case"])].append(row)
            for event in row.get("events", []):
                if isinstance(event, dict) and "samples" in event:
                    samples = event.pop("samples")
                    samples = samples[event.get("pre_frames", 0):]
                    if not samples:
                        event["missing_event"] = True
                        continue
                    event["sample_count"] = len(samples)
                    event["stats"] = summarize(samples, info["metrics"])
                    event["worst_frame_index"] = max(range(len(samples)), key=lambda index: samples[index][0])
                    fx_trace = event.pop("fx_profile_by_frame_us", [])
                    if fx_trace:
                        event["worst_frame_fx_us"] = fx_trace[event["worst_frame_index"]]
            record["rows"].append(row)
    for path in sorted((args.work / "run").glob("*/*/scene_gate.json")):
        phase, process, _ = path.relative_to(args.work / "run").parts
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        gate.append({"phase": phase, "process": process, "report": data})
    result["runs"] = runs
    result["rejected"] = rejected
    result["native_gate"] = gate
    result["groups"] = [
        {
            "phase": phase,
            "shield": shield,
            "case": case,
            "sessions": len(rows),
            "build_ms": [round(row["build_ms"], 3) for row in rows],
            "session_frame_medians": [row["stats"]["frame_ms"]["median"] for row in rows],
            "stats": {
                metric: {
                    stat: round((max if stat == "max" else statistics.median)(
                        row["stats"][metric][stat] for row in rows), 3)
                    for stat in ("median", "p95", "p99", "max")
                }
                for metric in rows[0]["stats"]
            },
        }
        for (phase, shield, case), rows in sorted(groups.items())
    ]
    write_json(args.out / "summary.json", result)
    write_baseline(args.out / "baseline.md", result["groups"])
    if not runs:
        raise ValueError("No runs were collected")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

// Node 18+, no dependencies. All child processes run from the repository root.
//
// Issue 358: the table tells the truth. A row has one of four words:
//   PASS  the check found zero failures inside the row
//   KNOWN only failures that sit on the baseline list, with the count
//   FAIL  anything else
//   SKIP  the check could not run on this machine (optional dependency)
// A PASS row never carries a failure count, a CHECK count or a differed count.
// A listed id that passes (or no longer runs) is an error until it is taken
// off the list. The pack CHECK count and the drift differed count are held
// against ceilings in checks_baseline.json that can only go down.

const ascii = s => String(s).replace(/[^\x20-\x7e\n\r\t]/g, '?');

// ---------- result-word rules (issue 358) ----------

function verdictLine(output) {
  const lines = String(output || '').split(/\r?\n/).map(l => l.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  for (let i = lines.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (/^(PASS|FAIL)\b/.test(lines[i])) return lines[i];
  return '';
}

function parseFindings(output) {
  const passIds = [], failIds = [];
  let summary = null;
  for (const raw of String(output || '').split(/\r?\n/)) {
    const line = raw.trim();
    let m = /^PASS\s+(\S+)(?:\s|$)/.exec(line);
    if (m) { passIds.push(m[1]); continue; }
    m = /^FAIL\s+(\S+)(?:\s|$)/.exec(line);
    if (m) { failIds.push(m[1]); continue; }
    m = /^(\d+)\s+tests,\s+(\d+)\s+pass,\s+(\d+)\s+fail/.exec(line);
    if (m) summary = { total: +m[1], pass: +m[2], fail: +m[3] };
  }
  return { passIds, failIds, summary };
}

function classifyFindings(run, baseline) {
  const { passIds, failIds, summary } = parseFindings(run.output);
  if (!summary) return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: missing findings summary' };
  if (passIds.length !== summary.pass || failIds.length !== summary.fail) {
    return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: parsed ' + passIds.length + ' pass / ' + failIds.length + ' fail lines, summary says ' + summary.pass + ' / ' + summary.fail };
  }
  const listed = new Set(baseline.knownFindingsFailures || []);
  const known = failIds.filter(id => listed.has(id));
  const unexpected = failIds.filter(id => !listed.has(id));
  const listedPasses = passIds.filter(id => listed.has(id));
  const seen = new Set([...passIds, ...failIds]);
  const listedMissing = [...listed].filter(id => !seen.has(id));
  if (listedPasses.length) return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: listed id(s) now pass, take them off the list: ' + listedPasses.join(', ') };
  if (unexpected.length) return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: ' + unexpected.length + ' new failure(s): ' + unexpected.join(', ') };
  if (listedMissing.length) return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: listed id(s) no longer run: ' + listedMissing.join(', ') };
  if (known.length) return { result: 'KNOWN', detail: 'KNOWN: ' + known.length + ' listed failure(s): ' + known.join(', ') };
  return { result: 'PASS', detail: 'PASS: all ' + summary.total + ' gated findings tests pass' };
}

  if (!m) return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: missing check pack summary' };
  const fails = +m[1], checks = +m[2];

const GUARD := preload("res://tools/ci/check_guard.gd")
const SHIP := preload("res://fx/fx_ship.gd")
const HULL := preload("res://fx/fx_hull.gd")

var failures := 0


func _init() -> void:
	GUARD.arm(self, "shield_cache_check")
	_run.call_deferred()


func _check(ok: bool, message: String) -> void:
	if not ok:
		failures += 1
		print("FAIL: ", message)


func _register(mesh: Mesh, facing: float, bob: float) -> Dictionary:
	var view := SV.new()
	root.add_child(view)
	view.code = "shield_fixture"
	view.rotation.y = facing
	view.position = Vector3(122, 0, -69)
	view.hull = Node3D.new()
	view.add_child(view.hull)
	view.hull.position.y = bob
	var part := MeshInstance3D.new()
	part.mesh = mesh
	view.hull.add_child(part)
	var core := Node3D.new()
	core.name = "hp_core"
	view.hull.add_child(core)
	var ship := SHIP.new()
	ship.root = view
	ship.meshes = [part]
	ship.hull = HULL.new()
	ship.hull.code = view.code
	ship.hull.analyse(view, ship.meshes, 1)
	var skin := ship._shield_skin()
	var hit := ship.shield_point(view.to_global(Vector3(0, 10, 0)))
	var result := {"bounds": ship.hull.box, "triangles": ship.hull.tri_count, "core": ship.hull.core,
		"skin": skin.get_faces() if skin != null else PackedVector3Array(),
		"hit": view.to_local(hit.p)}
	view.free()
	return result


func _run() -> void:
	var box := BoxMesh.new()
	box.size = Vector3(12, 3, 4)
	var first := _register(box, 0.0, 0.0)
	var turned := _register(box, TAU / 3.0, 0.0)
	var bobbed := _register(box, TAU / 3.0, 0.25)
	_check(SHIP._shield_skin_arrays.size() == 1, "facing and idle bob share a single cache entry")
	_check(not first.skin.is_empty() and first.skin == turned.skin and first.skin == bobbed.skin,
		"facing and idle bob keep the same fitted contour relative to the core")
	_check((bobbed.hit as Vector3).is_equal_approx((first.hit as Vector3) + Vector3.UP * 0.25),
		"the ray contact moves with the visible skin at registration")
	var arrays := box.surface_get_arrays(0)
	var verts: PackedVector3Array = arrays[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX]
	for i in verts.size():
		if verts[i].x > 0.0 and verts[i].y > 0.0:
			verts[i].y *= 0.5
	arrays[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX] = verts
	var replacement := ArrayMesh.new()
	replacement.add_surface_from_arrays(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES, arrays)
	var revised := _register(replacement, 0.0, 0.0)
	_check(first.bounds == revised.bounds and first.core == revised.core and first.triangles == revised.triangles,
		"replacement fixture collides under the original cache key")
	_check(SHIP._shield_skin_arrays.size() == 2 and not revised.skin.is_empty() and revised.skin != first.skin,
		"changed geometry with the same old key gets its own contour")
	var oldest = SHIP._shield_skin_arrays.keys()[0]
	for i in range(SHIP._shield_skin_arrays.size(), SHIP.SHIELD_SKIN_CACHE_LIMIT):
		SHIP._shield_skin_arrays[i] = []
	box.size.z += 0.5
	_register(box, 0.0, 0.0)
	_check(SHIP._shield_skin_arrays.size() == SHIP.SHIELD_SKIN_CACHE_LIMIT and not SHIP._shield_skin_arrays.has(oldest),
		"a new contour evicts the oldest entry when the cache is full")
	SHIP._shield_skin_arrays.clear()
	var puff := weakref(SV._puff_mat())
	var texture := weakref(SV._pm.albedo_texture)
	_check(puff.get_ref() != null and texture.get_ref() != null, "the live puff cache holds both resources")
	SV.clear_static()
	_check(puff.get_ref() == null and texture.get_ref() == null, "shutdown releases the cached puff material and texture")
	_check(SV._puff_mat().albedo_texture != null, "the puff material can be built again after cleanup")
	SV.clear_static()
	print("Shield cache and puff cleanup failures=%d" % failures)

+const GAS_CARD_SUPPORT := """
+vec2 gas_band(float band) {
+	return band < 0.5 ? vec2(-4.0, 2.0) : (band < 1.5 ? vec2(1.0, 8.0) : (band < 2.5 ? vec2(6.0, 14.0) : vec2(12.0, 18.0)));
+}
+float gas_layer(float band, float y) {
+	vec2 limits = gas_band(band);
+	return smoothstep(limits.x, limits.x + 1.5, y) * (1.0 - smoothstep(limits.y - 1.5, limits.y, y));
+}
+vec2 gas_card_offset(inout vec2 vertex, vec4 card, vec4 centre, mat4 inv_view, float height_scale) {
+	float angle = card.y * 6.2831;
+	mat2 spin = mat2(vec2(cos(angle), sin(angle)), vec2(-sin(angle), cos(angle)));
+#ifdef CLIP_GAS_CARD
+	// The radial falloff fits inside a disc. Bound that disc by its nonzero
+	// height band in the billboard plane before rasterizing the quad.
+	vec2 up = vec2(inv_view[0].y, inv_view[1].y);
+	float height_per_unit = length(up);
+	if (height_per_unit > 0.0001) {
+		up /= height_per_unit;
+		vec2 across = vec2(up.y, -up.x);
+		float centre_y = (inv_view * centre).y;
+		vec2 limits = (gas_band(floor(card.w)) * height_scale - centre_y) / (height_per_unit * card.x);
+		// Add a small margin for rounding at the height edges. The fragment
+		// shader still applies the original radial and height fades.
+		limits = clamp(limits + vec2(-0.0001, 0.0001), -0.5, 0.5);
+		vec2 offset = across * vertex.x + up * mix(limits.x, limits.y, vertex.y + 0.5);
+		// The soft intersection uses Godot's interpolated VERTEX.z. Keep its
+		// original quad coordinate even though POSITION draws a clipped quad.
+		vertex = transpose(spin) * offset;
+		return offset;
+	}
+#endif
+	return spin * vertex;
+}
+"""

## The seats: who does what and how each is started (rewritten Nov 15 2026 from the Nov 14 update, R250; older seat text is in docs/archive/LOOP_history_2026-11-14.md)

Ryan, on what a hand-over must carry: "That also includes how we use deepseek, codex, muse, our evaluation of Kimi, etc." This section is the live truth for seats; RULEBOOK 2.6 holds the rules behind it. Lines marked "observation" are the Board's notes, not Ryan's rules: revise them with evidence.

- **Seat order (Ryan, Nov 13, R242).** DeepSeek for small, well-specified jobs; Sonnet API for mid-size code and UI; Opus (API arm or a plan-side worker) for Blender and large or open-ended work; Codex only for what no other seat can do; Kimi by results. Today's departures from that order follow from the API credit being spent (below). Any job that runs the full checks gets a cap of 90 minutes or more (a Board note, not Ryan's words).
- **The Board.** One Claude thread in the Claude Code Project, Opus 5.5 at high effort (Ryan, Nov 16). Judgement, reviews, merges, specs, picks put to Ryan; its duties are the section above. No Fable advisor is visible in the Project Board thread (Nov 16); R252 applies if one comes back.
- **Opus 5.5 workers (plan side).** On (R330, Ryan Nov 19 14:17 UTC: usage reset on a bigger plan, "rock and roll with opus helpers and kick through all this backlog"; earlier R253). Every Blender ship build is Opus's again (R205); Codex keeps pipeline, effects and capture jobs. Each is its own thread in the Claude Code Project, started by the Board: a fresh cloud copy of the repo with the voidsworn cloud environment (Godot 4.7.2 headless, selected by Ryan Nov 16), branch opus/issue-N, never merges its own PR (RULEBOOK 2.2), the PC through the Board (R334, below). As many threads as the Board can review well (R330; normally two or three); propose any big new thread to Ryan first (project instructions). What we learned: give them Ryan's words and the one requirement that outranks the numbers; tell them which checks their change will trip; demand named pictures no taller than 720 px; a worker that finishes very fast gets its work sampled before it is trusted.
- **API arms `opus` and `sonnet` (work_issue.bat N opus|sonnet): OFF** until the Claude API credit's monthly refresh, about Nov 21; Ryan adds no credit (R250 item 1). When on: Sonnet for well-specified code and UI (won the issue 652 head to head: cleaner fix, $3.23 against $9.08), Opus for open-ended or Blender jobs. Same model family as the Board, so never the different-model check of Opus work (R219).
- **Codex** (gpt-6.2-sol pinned in tools/pc/codex_issue.bat since Ryan, Nov 17; reviews stay on 6.1 Terra; RULEBOOK 2.7; local on the PC only, no cloud tasks). On the Pro plan since Nov 15 11:33 CST (R264: "significant usage upgrade"); usage moves slowly because most of a run waits on captures. Pipeline, effects, terrain, capture and Godot UI jobs. FOUR LANES (R301, Nov 16: lane D added, code only), each with its own tools copy, repo and mirror: the main chain (build_b, board\repo, repo-mirror.git: GPU jobs), lane B (build_c, board_b\repo, repo-mirror-b.git: Godot UI and lighter capture jobs) and lane C (build_d, board_c\repo, repo-mirror-c.git: code-only jobs, no GPU; R268, no Codex cloud because its model cannot be pinned) and lane D (build_e, a copy of build_d\tools, board_d\repo: code-only jobs, no GPU; R301; status codex_lane_d*.txt). Status files: codex_chain_*.txt, codex_lane_b.txt, codex_lane_c.txt in the PC root. Never start two runs on the same lane's tools: they share one repo folder and the second replaces the first's checkout. Launch: a chain .bat that calls the lane's codex_issue.bat per issue with the default six-hour CODEX_CAP ceiling and 30-minute STALL_MIN after issue 818 deployment (replaces the old cap defaults in Known traps), queued through queue\q_*.bat. Codex reads gpu_go.txt (first line "GPU cleared") before GPU captures. it was the main builder for one day on Nov 14, Blender included (R250), a stand-in that ended when Opus workers came back (R253). Observation: about 3 or 4 big jobs per 5 hour window; it stops with "usage limit" and names the reset time. The Board sets effort per job (high fit more jobs in a window on Nov 14). One job per lane; only the main chain takes GPU jobs. Launch: labels codex AND blocked on the issue; commit a run file to the PC root that calls "%USERPROFILE%\Downloads\voidsworn_test\build_b\tools\pc\codex_issue.bat" N (chain several N in one file, as CODEX_CHAIN_14H2.bat does, with a log line per job and a findstr for "usage limit"), and queue\q_codex_N.bat that `start`s it, CRLF. After a limit, a waiting run file (timeout until the reset). Results: board\issue-N\ (result.txt, last.md, log.txt, shots\). Image jobs need no GPU, 10 to 15 minutes per six pictures. What we learned: briefed in words it drifts on shapes; its reports keep observed and inferred apart.
- **Kimi: no longer a seat** (R257, Ryan Nov 15: "Kimi is maxed out until 12/12. I just cancelled."). Its jobs went to DeepSeek (41, 371). Nothing is sent to Kimi; KIMI_15F's quota loop on the PC gives up by itself.
- **DeepSeek workhorse** (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash in OpenCode, arm `deepseek`). Small, exact jobs: rules, tests, scripts, screens to a spec. After issue 818 deployment, STALL_MIN defaults to 30 minutes without progress and WORK_CAP defaults to a six-hour ceiling (it waits on long PC commands, which costs no tokens). Launch: WORKHORSE_FLASH_N.bat calling work217\tools\work_issue.bat N deepseek, branch work/issue-N-deepseek fixed in the issue first. Explicit WORK_CAP values still set the ceiling; remove old 7200 overrides to use the new default. It needs a tight brief and the Board reads its diff.
- **Muse** (Rey chairs; a blind Rey leg first on research, design and review jobs, R89; legs from DeepSeek, Qwen, Grok and Google Flash in every action, R231). Design, research, concept pictures, outside checks of Opus-built work and audits (706). Muse starts its own runs (Ryan, Nov 17 03:55 UTC: "It starts its own runs now"): its watcher polls the board every 2 minutes through Muse's scoped GitHub token and picks up muse-labelled issues, Board briefs, merges and change requests; Ryan no longer starts each run and nothing needs posting on 256 first. Every Muse branch gets a PR (auto_pr, Nov 17); muse/wip-* opts out. Grok legs are back (PR 938 had one, Nov 17). What we learned: its image models drift on layout and counts but suit organic shapes and edits of a liked picture; keep the Board's workers' output away from it while it is the outside check.
- **Dispatch (all seats, Nov 16 2026, issue 880).** The claim is the running label plus the status comment, set before
  work starts (RULEBOOK 2.4); a seat that finds a job claimed, or its delivery branch already on GitHub, does not run it
  and tells the Board (872 ran twice in one morning without it). Artoo's standing job (issue 906) includes a dispatch sweep
  before each Board queueing round: open issues with merged PRs, briefs living only in comments, stale LOOP and HANDOFF
  lines. The sweep is the audit; the mechanisms are the same-step close (R288) and the body brief (R281). Runner resource
  handling is its own contract, not a courtesy: wait and retry on a held file (882), truthful failure reporting (873),
  and the kept-checkout cap; the 5 and 10 minute chain gaps and the hand stops are patches that retire when those land.
- **PC chores are the Board's own (Ryan, Nov 13).** Runner settings, smoke tests, copies of runner files: the Board writes the change and a small .bat, queues it, reads the log back. The bridge has file tools only (device_bash fails: hardware virtualisation is off in the BIOS). No heavy job while Ryan is playing; when he games, stop only what loses nothing and restart when he says. Never delete anything on the PC.
- **Artoo** (Ryan's ChatGPT dot, OpenAI cloud). Independent technical reviewer (R295, RULEBOOK 2.7): comments by itself on PRs and issues, general sweeps on issue 906; merge issues, bugs and technical problems only, never design or taste. Each comment starts "Artoo (technical review):" (it posts through Ryan's account) and names the commit it read. Never pushes, merges, closes or relabels; the Board checks each finding against live main and replies with what it did.
- **Ryan.** Picks, looks, money. (Muse starts its own runs since Nov 17, see its seat line.) The PC is his; GPU work is sized to the job and the RTX 5080, not a fixed count (R293, RULEBOOK 3.4; issue 896 makes the slot tool follow).
- **Not taken (R250):** Gemini 4 Hydrogen; a pay-as-you-go Gemini 4 Carbon trial on one job before Nov 30 is Ryan's call, not queued.

"""Build the battle and storm sheets from the second capture of each source."""

import argparse
import json
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image, ImageChops, ImageDraw, ImageFont, ImageStat

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))
from picture_provenance import Review, digest, save_picture, verify

STAGE = "installed in game"
BATTLE = (
    ("battle_170", "Battle view, radius 170"),
    ("battle_26", "Close view, radius 26"),
    ("shield_hit", "First shield hit, radius 26"),
    ("first_wreck", "First wreck frame, radius 26"),
)
STORM = (
    ("storm_high_170", "storm_max_170", "Strike, radius 170"),
    ("storm_high_26", "storm_max_26", "Cloud detail, radius 26"),
)


def load_capture(folder, name, source):
    capture = folder / f"{name}.png"
    marked = folder / f"{name}_source.png"
    capture_date = datetime.fromtimestamp(capture.stat().st_mtime, timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    with Image.open(capture) as image:
        save_picture(image, marked, STAGE, sources=[{
            **source, "picture_name": capture.name, "stage": STAGE,
            "date": capture_date, "image_sha256": digest(capture.read_bytes()),
            "sources": [source],
        }])
    return marked


def sheet(title, rows, output):
    review = Review(STAGE)
    image = Image.new("RGB", (1280, 720), "#10151e")
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)
    title_font = ImageFont.truetype("C:/Windows/Fonts/segoeuib.ttf", 29)
    label_font = ImageFont.truetype("C:/Windows/Fonts/segoeui.ttf", 19)
    code_font = ImageFont.truetype("C:/Windows/Fonts/segoeui.ttf", 16)
    draw.text((22, 17), title, font=title_font, fill="#fff0de")
    draw.text((24, 55), output.stem, font=code_font, fill="#ffbe8b")
    for i, (label, pair) in enumerate(rows):
        if len(rows) == 2:
            x, y, width, gap = 194, 80 + i * 264, 376, 512
        else:
            x, y, width, gap = 22 + (i % 2) * 630, 100 + (i // 2) * 252, 300, 309
        draw.text((x, y), label, font=label_font, fill="#fff0de")
        for col, (name, path) in enumerate(pair):
            start = x + col * gap
            draw.text((start, y + 27), name, font=code_font, fill="#ffbe8b")
            capture = review.open(path).convert("RGB")
            image.paste(capture.resize((width, round(width * 9 / 16)), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS), (start, y + 49))
    review.save(image, output, quality=96)
    verify(output)


def compare(one, two):
    with Image.open(one) as a, Image.open(two) as b:
        difference = ImageChops.difference(a.convert("RGB"), b.convert("RGB"))
        stats = ImageStat.Stat(difference)
        return {"mean_rgb_of_255": stats.mean, "max_rgb_of_255": [max(v) for v in stats.extrema]}


def provenance(work):
    build = json.loads((work / "godot/build_info.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
    diff = work / "source_diff.sha256"
    source = {"source_commit": build["commit"], "source_dirty": diff.is_file(),
              "source_diff_sha256": diff.read_text().strip() if diff.is_file() else "", "stage": STAGE}
    if not source["source_dirty"]:
        source["source_commit_date"] = build["commit_date"]
    return source


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("before", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("after", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("results", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--label", default="proof")
    options = parser.parse_args()
    before = provenance(options.before)
    after = provenance(options.after)
    before_take = options.before / f"{options.label}_2"
    after_take = options.after / f"{options.label}_2"
    battle = []
    differences = {}
    for name, label in BATTLE:
        battle.append((label, (("Before", load_capture(before_take, name, before)),
                               ("After", load_capture(after_take, name, after)))))
        files = [work / f"{options.label}_{take}" / f"{name}.png"
                 for work in (options.before, options.after) for take in (1, 2)]
        differences[name] = {"before_repeat": compare(files[0], files[1]),
                             "after_repeat": compare(files[2], files[3]),
                             "before_after": compare(files[1], files[3])}
    storm = [(label, (("High", load_capture(before_take, a, before)),
                      ("Max", load_capture(before_take, b, before))))
             for a, b, label in STORM]
    sheet("Scene 207   /   V1b_r_23", battle, options.output / "PERF1070_RUN2_BATTLE.jpg")
    sheet("Dense storm   /   seed 4103", storm, options.output / "PERF1070_RUN2_STORM.jpg")
    options.results.write_text(json.dumps(differences, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
