+# Issue 1070 performance evidence
+
+The [Run 2 report](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/README.md) has the original timings, raw traces and reproduction steps. [Battle comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_BATTLE.jpg) · [High and Max storm comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_STORM.jpg)
+
+## Run 3 cost baseline on main
+
+Main revision `0c41f332c956040112361444597d02be99a40b75` contains the content-keyed fitted shield cache from issue 1130. Run 3 uses the preserved Run 2 fleet. All 259 installed ship files matched the installed manifest, and both the ship and generated asset manifests matched Run 2. The replay probe follows main's scene-gate build signature and keeps Run 2's event sequence, sampling windows and three-minute load allowance. The first attempt hit main's one-minute timeout before sampling.
+
+The reference is for the flagship death (#1077), shield failure (#1078) and nebula wake (#1079). Use the same case, resolution, camera and timer when comparing a prototype. First-use results use 1080p Max and a fresh Godot process per session. The steady Scene 207 case uses 20 hulls and four launch wings, seeded volleys and the engagement camera. The dense storm case uses seed 4103, 31 storm hexes and 28 nebula hexes at radius 170. Its ships are idle and its weather runs live. The 4K cases render the 3D scene at 3840×2160 in the same 1920×1080 window.
+
+### Cold start at 1080p Max
+
+Each cell gives the median of the three session peaks and the worst frame across the three sessions, in ms. The first-hit row uses the full 2.3-second Run 2 window. The wreck row covers the submission frame and two frames on either side.
+
+| Event | Shield | Run 2 patched | Run 3 on main |
+|---|---|---:|---:|
+| First shield hit window | Fitted | 8.049 / 9.382 | 30.266 / 44.393 |
+| First shield failure | Fitted | 8.090 / 8.753 | 7.443 / 9.230 |
+| First death and aftermath | Fitted | 12.947 / 13.868 | 13.066 / 13.598 |
+| First wreck submission | Fitted | 9.030 / 13.868 | 9.840 / 12.076 |
+| First shield hit window | Egg | 8.627 / 11.032 | 25.276 / 38.524 |
+| First shield failure | Egg | 8.699 / 13.230 | 9.300 / 10.200 |
+| First death and aftermath | Egg | 15.579 / 22.908 | 12.418 / 20.152 |
+
+The first five fitted draw frames peaked at 8.254 ms across the three launches. The fitted window's 27.120 to 44.393 ms peaks began 783 to 972 ms after dispatch, after the fitted shield's glow expired. The egg also showed later peaks. At the longest fitted frame, the main process callbacks took 2.819 ms, render CPU took 2.139 ms and GPU took 2.281 ms. Pipeline counters stayed flat in all six shield-hit windows.
+
+### Scene 207 and dense storm on main
+
+Three fitted sessions per case, with 180 warm-up frames and at least 720 measured frames and eight seconds. Frame median and p99 are the medians across sessions. Worst is the longest individual frame. GPU median is the median of the session medians. Times are in ms.
+
+| Fixture | Resolution | Frame median | Frame p99 | Worst frame | GPU median |
+|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Scene 207 Max | 1080p | 8.329 | 16.166 | 58.463 | 2.508 |
+| Scene 207 Max | 4K | 7.444 | 18.001 | 50.535 | 5.576 |
+| Dense storm Max | 1080p | 2.395 | 4.424 | 6.780 | 1.695 |
+| Dense storm High | 1080p | 2.415 | 5.245 | 11.699 | 1.886 |
+| Dense storm Max | 4K | 5.802 | 7.642 | 17.741 | 5.208 |
+| Dense storm High | 4K | 7.147 | 8.642 | 9.305 | 6.732 |
+
+Scene 207 passed the 12.5 ms gate at both resolutions, using the 1080p frame median and 4K GPU median. Both resolutions exceeded Run 2's 50 ms worst-frame mark. The longest 1080p frame spent 50.938 ms in main process callbacks, with 2.768 ms on the GPU and no new pipeline builds. Its 4K counterpart spent 44.774 ms in main process callbacks, with 5.587 ms on the GPU.
+
+The storm comparison and shield-hit control are in progress.

 # Issue 232 E17/NB5 sheet: the live weight, overridable for the three-weight capture (default is the shipped 0.25).
 var faction_end_weight := clampf(float(OS.get_environment("VS_NEB_W")), 0.0, NEBULA_FACTION_END_WEIGHT) if OS.get_environment("VS_NEB_W") != "" else NEBULA_FACTION_END_WEIGHT
 
+const GAS_CARD_SUPPORT := """
+const float MIN_GAS_DENSITY = 0.002;
+// Leave room for rounding when an upper bound drops an empty fragment early.
+const float GAS_DENSITY_BOUND = MIN_GAS_DENSITY * 0.95;
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+float gas_noise_floor(float lo, float hi, float max_density) {
+	// smoothstep(t) is at most 3 * t * t. Below this noise value, even
+	// the strongest possible footprint and contact cannot reach the cutoff.
+	return mix(lo, hi, sqrt(GAS_DENSITY_BOUND / (3.0 * max_density)));
+}
+#endif
+vec2 gas_band(float band) {
+	return band < 0.5 ? vec2(-4.0, 2.0) : (band < 1.5 ? vec2(1.0, 8.0) : (band < 2.5 ? vec2(6.0, 14.0) : vec2(12.0, 18.0)));
+}
+float gas_layer(float band, float y) {
+	vec2 limits = gas_band(band);
+	return smoothstep(limits.x, limits.x + 1.5, y) * (1.0 - smoothstep(limits.y - 1.5, limits.y, y));
+}
+vec2 gas_card_offset(inout vec2 vertex, vec4 card, vec4 centre, mat4 inv_view, float height_scale) {
+	float angle = card.y * 6.2831;
+	mat2 spin = mat2(vec2(cos(angle), sin(angle)), vec2(-sin(angle), cos(angle)));
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+	// The radial falloff fits inside a disc. Bound that disc by its nonzero
+	// height band in the billboard plane before rasterizing the quad.
+	vec2 up = vec2(inv_view[0].y, inv_view[1].y);
+	float height_per_unit = length(up);
+	if (height_per_unit > 0.0001) {
+		up /= height_per_unit;
+		vec2 across = vec2(up.y, -up.x);
+		float centre_y = (inv_view * centre).y;
+		vec2 limits = (gas_band(floor(card.w)) * height_scale - centre_y) / (height_per_unit * card.x);
+		// Add a small margin for rounding at the height edges. The fragment
+		// shader still applies the original radial and height fades.
+		limits = clamp(limits + vec2(-0.0001, 0.0001), -0.5, 0.5);
+		vec2 offset = across * vertex.x + up * mix(limits.x, limits.y, vertex.y + 0.5);
+		// The soft intersection uses Godot's interpolated VERTEX.z. Keep its
+		// original quad coordinate even though POSITION draws a clipped quad.
+		vertex = transpose(spin) * offset;
+		return offset;
+	}
+#endif
+	return spin * vertex;
+}
+"""
+

+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+float wh31_corner(vec3 p, float offset) { p += offset; return fract((p.x + p.y) * p.z); }
+#endif
 float wvn3(vec3 x) {
 	vec3 i = floor(x); vec3 f = fract(x); f = f * f * (3.0 - 2.0 * f);
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+	// Each pair of corners above one another shares the x and z terms of
+	// dot(p, p.zyx + 31.32). Each plane shares one y term.
+	vec3 lo = fract(i * 0.1031);
+	vec3 hi = fract((i + vec3(1.0)) * 0.1031);
+	vec3 lo_bias = lo + 31.32;
+	vec3 hi_bias = hi + 31.32;
+	vec4 xz = vec4(lo.x, hi.x, lo.x, hi.x) * vec4(lo_bias.zz, hi_bias.zz)
+		+ vec4(lo.zz, hi.zz) * vec4(lo_bias.x, hi_bias.x, lo_bias.x, hi_bias.x);
+	vec2 y = vec2(lo.y, hi.y) * vec2(lo_bias.y, hi_bias.y);
+	vec4 front = vec4(wh31_corner(lo, xz.x + y.x),
+		wh31_corner(vec3(hi.x, lo.yz), xz.y + y.x),
+		wh31_corner(vec3(lo.x, hi.y, lo.z), xz.x + y.y),
+		wh31_corner(vec3(hi.xy, lo.z), xz.y + y.y));
+	vec4 back = vec4(wh31_corner(vec3(lo.xy, hi.z), xz.z + y.x),
+		wh31_corner(vec3(hi.x, lo.y, hi.z), xz.w + y.x),
+		wh31_corner(vec3(lo.x, hi.yz), xz.z + y.y), wh31_corner(hi, xz.w + y.y));
+	return mix(mix(mix(front.x, front.y, f.x), mix(front.z, front.w, f.x), f.y),
+		mix(mix(back.x, back.y, f.x), mix(back.z, back.w, f.x), f.y), f.z);
+#else

+# Issue 1070 performance evidence
+
+The [Run 2 report](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/README.md) has the original timings, raw traces and reproduction steps. [Battle comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_BATTLE.jpg) · [High and Max storm comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_STORM.jpg)
+
+## Run 3 cost baseline on main
+
+Main revision `0c41f332c956040112361444597d02be99a40b75` contains the content-keyed fitted shield cache from issue 1130. Run 3 uses the preserved Run 2 fleet. All 259 installed ship files matched the installed manifest, and both the ship and generated asset manifests matched Run 2. The replay probe follows main's scene-gate build signature and keeps Run 2's event sequence, sampling windows and three-minute load allowance. The first attempt hit main's one-minute timeout before sampling.
+
+The reference is for the flagship death (#1077), shield failure (#1078) and nebula wake (#1079). Use the same case, resolution, camera and timer when comparing a prototype. First-use results use 1080p Max and a fresh Godot process per session. The steady Scene 207 case uses 20 hulls and four launch wings, seeded volleys and the engagement camera. The dense storm case uses seed 4103, 31 storm hexes and 28 nebula hexes at radius 170. Its ships are idle and its weather runs live. The 4K cases render the 3D scene at 3840×2160 in the same 1920×1080 window.
+
+### Cold start at 1080p Max
+
+Each cell gives the median of the three session peaks and the worst frame across the three sessions, in ms. The first-hit row uses the full 2.3-second Run 2 window. The wreck row covers the submission frame and two frames on either side.
+
+| Event | Shield | Run 2 patched | Run 3 on main |
+|---|---|---:|---:|
+| First shield hit window | Fitted | 8.049 / 9.382 | 30.266 / 44.393 |
+| First shield failure | Fitted | 8.090 / 8.753 | 7.443 / 9.230 |
+| First death and aftermath | Fitted | 12.947 / 13.868 | 13.066 / 13.598 |
+| First wreck submission | Fitted | 9.030 / 13.868 | 9.840 / 12.076 |
+| First shield hit window | Egg | 8.627 / 11.032 | 25.276 / 38.524 |
+| First shield failure | Egg | 8.699 / 13.230 | 9.300 / 10.200 |
+| First death and aftermath | Egg | 15.579 / 22.908 | 12.418 / 20.152 |
+
+The first five fitted draw frames peaked at 8.254 ms across the three launches. The fitted window's 27.120 to 44.393 ms peaks began 783 to 972 ms after dispatch, after the fitted shield's glow expired. The egg also showed later peaks. At the longest fitted frame, the main process callbacks took 2.819 ms, render CPU took 2.139 ms and GPU took 2.281 ms. Pipeline counters stayed flat in all six shield-hit windows.
+
+Two controls skipped the first shield hit and kept the shield hidden through the same 2.3-second window. They still peaked at 40.783 and 22.952 ms. The intervals before the first process callback were 34.579 and 18.889 ms, respectively. The hit-enabled control peaked at 21.057 ms, with 17.848 ms before the first callback. These later gaps explain the over-20 ms samples in the shield-hit window. An aborted headless fixture check was still running during the first batch. It was closed before these controls, and the complete main batch is being repeated.
+
+### Scene 207 and dense storm on main
+
+Three fitted sessions per case, with 180 warm-up frames and at least 720 measured frames and eight seconds. Frame median and p99 are the medians across sessions. Worst is the longest individual frame. GPU median is the median of the session medians. Times are in ms.
+
+| Fixture | Resolution | Frame median | Frame p99 | Worst frame | GPU median |
+|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Scene 207 Max | 1080p | 8.329 | 16.166 | 58.463 | 2.508 |
+| Scene 207 Max | 4K | 7.444 | 18.001 | 50.535 | 5.576 |
+| Dense storm Max | 1080p | 2.395 | 4.424 | 6.780 | 1.695 |
+| Dense storm High | 1080p | 2.415 | 5.245 | 11.699 | 1.886 |
+| Dense storm Max | 4K | 5.802 | 7.642 | 17.741 | 5.208 |
+| Dense storm High | 4K | 7.147 | 8.642 | 9.305 | 6.732 |
+
+Scene 207 passed the 12.5 ms gate at both resolutions, using the 1080p frame median and 4K GPU median. Both resolutions exceeded Run 2's 50 ms worst-frame mark. The longest 1080p frame spent 50.938 ms in main process callbacks, with 2.768 ms on the GPU and no new pipeline builds. Its 4K counterpart spent 44.774 ms in main process callbacks, with 5.587 ms on the GPU.
+
+The storm comparison and baseline repeat are in progress. [Raw traces and session summaries](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/raw/run3/)

+const GAS_CARD_SUPPORT := """
+const float MIN_GAS_DENSITY = 0.002;
+// Leave room for rounding when an upper bound drops an empty fragment early.
+const float GAS_DENSITY_BOUND = MIN_GAS_DENSITY * 0.95;
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+float gas_noise_floor(float lo, float hi, float max_density) {
+	// smoothstep(t) is at most 3 * t * t. Below this noise value, even
+	// the strongest possible footprint and contact cannot reach the cutoff.
+	return mix(lo, hi, sqrt(GAS_DENSITY_BOUND / (3.0 * max_density)));
+}
+#endif
+vec2 gas_band(float band) {
+	return band < 0.5 ? vec2(-4.0, 2.0) : (band < 1.5 ? vec2(1.0, 8.0) : (band < 2.5 ? vec2(6.0, 14.0) : vec2(12.0, 18.0)));
+}
+float gas_layer(float band, float y) {
+	vec2 limits = gas_band(band);
+	return smoothstep(limits.x, limits.x + 1.5, y) * (1.0 - smoothstep(limits.y - 1.5, limits.y, y));
+}
+vec2 gas_card_offset(inout vec2 vertex, vec4 card, vec4 centre, mat4 inv_view, float height_scale) {
+	float angle = card.y * 6.2831;
+	mat2 spin = mat2(vec2(cos(angle), sin(angle)), vec2(-sin(angle), cos(angle)));
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+	// The radial falloff fits inside a disc. Bound that disc by its nonzero
+	// height band in the billboard plane before rasterizing the quad.
+	vec2 up = vec2(inv_view[0].y, inv_view[1].y);
+	float height_per_unit = length(up);
+	if (height_per_unit > 0.0001) {
+		up /= height_per_unit;
+		vec2 across = vec2(up.y, -up.x);
+		float centre_y = (inv_view * centre).y;
+		vec2 limits = (gas_band(floor(card.w)) * height_scale - centre_y) / (height_per_unit * card.x);
+		// Add a small margin for rounding at the height edges. The fragment
+		// shader still applies the original radial and height fades.
+		limits = clamp(limits + vec2(-0.0001, 0.0001), -0.5, 0.5);
+		vec2 offset = across * vertex.x + up * mix(limits.x, limits.y, vertex.y + 0.5);
+		// The soft intersection uses Godot's interpolated VERTEX.z. Keep its
+		// original quad coordinate even though POSITION draws a clipped quad.
+		vertex = transpose(spin) * offset;
+		return offset;
+	}
+#endif
+	return spin * vertex;
+}
+"""

 float wfbm(vec2 p) { float a = 0.5; float s = 0.0; for (int k = 0; k < 5; k++) { s += a * wvn(p); p = p * 2.03 + vec2(1.7, 9.2); a *= 0.5; } return s; }
 // r6: Hoskins' hash13 (the old product hash drew diagonal lattice lines once a shader amplified the noise)
 float wh31(vec3 p) { p = fract(p * 0.1031); p += dot(p, p.zyx + 31.32); return fract((p.x + p.y) * p.z); }
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+float wh31_corner(vec3 p, float offset) { p += offset; return fract((p.x + p.y) * p.z); }
+#endif
 float wvn3(vec3 x) {
 	vec3 i = floor(x); vec3 f = fract(x); f = f * f * (3.0 - 2.0 * f);
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+	// Each pair of corners above one another shares the x and z terms of
+	// dot(p, p.zyx + 31.32). Each plane shares one y term.
+	vec3 lo = fract(i * 0.1031);
+	vec3 hi = fract((i + vec3(1.0)) * 0.1031);
+	vec3 lo_bias = lo + 31.32;
+	vec3 hi_bias = hi + 31.32;
+	vec4 xz = vec4(lo.x, hi.x, lo.x, hi.x) * vec4(lo_bias.zz, hi_bias.zz)
+		+ vec4(lo.zz, hi.zz) * vec4(lo_bias.x, hi_bias.x, lo_bias.x, hi_bias.x);
+	vec2 y = vec2(lo.y, hi.y) * vec2(lo_bias.y, hi_bias.y);
+	vec4 front = vec4(wh31_corner(lo, xz.x + y.x),
+		wh31_corner(vec3(hi.x, lo.yz), xz.y + y.x),
+		wh31_corner(vec3(lo.x, hi.y, lo.z), xz.x + y.y),
+		wh31_corner(vec3(hi.xy, lo.z), xz.y + y.y));
+	vec4 back = vec4(wh31_corner(vec3(lo.xy, hi.z), xz.z + y.x),
+		wh31_corner(vec3(hi.x, lo.y, hi.z), xz.w + y.x),
+		wh31_corner(vec3(lo.x, hi.yz), xz.z + y.y), wh31_corner(hi, xz.w + y.y));
+	return mix(mix(mix(front.x, front.y, f.x), mix(front.z, front.w, f.x), f.y),
+		mix(mix(back.x, back.y, f.x), mix(back.z, back.w, f.x), f.y), f.z);
+#else
 	return mix(mix(mix(wh31(i), wh31(i + vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)), f.x), mix(wh31(i + vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)), wh31(i + vec3(1.0, 1.0, 0.0)), f.x), f.y),
 		mix(mix(wh31(i + vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)), wh31(i + vec3(1.0, 0.0, 1.0)), f.x), mix(wh31(i + vec3(0.0, 1.0, 1.0)), wh31(i + vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)), f.x), f.y), f.z);
+#endif
 }
 float wfbm3(vec3 p) { float a = 0.5; float s = 0.0; for (int k = 0; k < 5; k++) { s += a * wvn3(p); p = p * 2.03 + 3.1; a *= 0.5; } return s; }
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+// Each octave is in [0, 1]. If even the remaining octaves at full
+// strength cannot reach the threshold, the caller's smoothstep is zero.
+float wfbm3_above(vec3 p, float threshold) {
+	float a = 0.5;
+	float s = 0.0;
+	float remaining = 0.96875;
+	for (int k = 0; k < 5; k++) {
+		s += a * wvn3(p);
+		remaining -= a;
+		if (k >= 1 && k < 4 && s + remaining + 0.00001 < threshold) { return 0.0; }
+		p = p * 2.03 + 3.1;
+		a *= 0.5;
+	}
+	return s;
+}
+#endif
 """

extends SceneTree
# Issue 368. Deterministic CPU bake; no rendering and no external assets.
# godot --headless --path godot --script res://world/nebula_noise_bake.gd
const SIDE := 128

func _initialize() -> void:
	var noise := FastNoiseLite.new()
	noise.seed = 368
	noise.noise_type = FastNoiseLite.TYPE_SIMPLEX_SMOOTH
	noise.frequency = 0.045
	noise.fractal_octaves = 4
	var slices: Array[Image] = []
	for z in SIDE:
		var data := PackedByteArray()
		data.resize(SIDE * SIDE)
		for y in SIDE:
			for x in SIDE:
				# Blend across opposite faces, so the baked field tiles in all three axes.
				var value := 0.0
				var p := Vector3(x, y, z)
				var t := p / float(SIDE)
				for corner in 8:
					var c := Vector3(corner & 1, (corner >> 1) & 1, (corner >> 2) & 1)
					var weight := Vector3.ONE - t
					if c.x > 0: weight.x = t.x
					if c.y > 0: weight.y = t.y
					if c.z > 0: weight.z = t.z
					var q := p - c * SIDE
					value += noise.get_noise_3dv(q) * weight.x * weight.y * weight.z
				data[y * SIDE + x] = clampi(roundi((value * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255.0), 0, 255)
		slices.append(Image.create_from_data(SIDE, SIDE, false, Image.FORMAT_R8, data))
	var volume = load("res://world/nebula_noise_data.gd").new()
	volume.slices = slices
	var error := ResourceSaver.save(volume, "res://world/nebula_noise.res", ResourceSaver.FLAG_COMPRESS)
	print("NEBULA_NOISE 128x128x128 R8 seed 368 result ", error)
	quit(0 if error == OK else 1)

# CPU-backed 3D texture source. Baking must also work with Godot's headless renderer.
@export var side := 128
@export var seed_value := 368
@export var slices: Array[Image] = []

func texture() -> ImageTexture3D:
	var result := ImageTexture3D.new()
	if slices.size() != side:
		push_error("Issue 368: missing noise slices")
		return null
	var error := result.create(Image.FORMAT_R8, side, side, side, false, slices)
	if error != OK:
		push_error("Issue 368: cannot upload noise texture: %s" % error)
		return null
	return result

from pathlib import Path
import sys
import numpy as np

size = 96
x_range = np.arange(-48, -48 + size, dtype=np.float32)
y_range = np.arange(-32, -32 + size, dtype=np.float32)
z_range = x_range
x = x_range[None, None, :] * np.float32(0.1031)
y = y_range[None, :, None] * np.float32(0.1031)
z = z_range[:, None, None] * np.float32(0.1031)
x -= np.floor(x)
y -= np.floor(y)
z -= np.floor(z)
bias = np.float32(31.32)
cross = (z * (x + bias)).astype(np.float32)
cross = (y.astype(np.float64) * (y + bias) + cross).astype(np.float32)
cross = (x.astype(np.float64) * (z + bias) + cross).astype(np.float32)
out = ((x + cross) + (y + cross)) * (z + cross)
(out - np.floor(out)).astype('<f4').tofile(sys.argv[1])

+# Issue 1070 performance evidence
+
+The [Run 2 report](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/README.md) has the original timings, raw traces and reproduction steps. [Battle comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_BATTLE.jpg) · [High and Max storm comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_STORM.jpg)
+
+## Run 3 cost baseline on main
+
+Main revision `0c41f332c956040112361444597d02be99a40b75` contains the content-keyed fitted shield cache from issue 1130. Run 3 uses the preserved Run 2 fleet. All 259 installed ship files matched the installed manifest, and both the ship and generated asset manifests matched Run 2. The replay probe follows main's scene-gate build signature and keeps Run 2's event sequence, sampling windows and three-minute load allowance. The first attempt hit main's one-minute timeout before sampling.
+
+The reference is for the flagship death (#1077), shield failure (#1078) and nebula wake (#1079). Use the same case, resolution, camera and timer when comparing a prototype. First-use results use 1080p Max and a fresh Godot process per session. The steady Scene 207 case uses 20 hulls and four launch wings, seeded volleys and the engagement camera. The dense storm case uses seed 4103, 31 storm hexes and 28 nebula hexes at radius 170. Its ships are idle and its weather runs live. The 4K cases render the 3D scene at 3840×2160 in the same 1920×1080 window.
+
+### Cold start at 1080p Max
+
+Each cell gives the median of the three session peaks and the worst frame across the three sessions, in ms. The first-hit row uses the full 2.3-second Run 2 window. The wreck row covers the submission frame and two frames on either side.
+
+| Event | Shield | Run 2 patched | Run 3 on main |
+|---|---|---:|---:|
+| First shield hit window | Fitted | 8.049 / 9.382 | 30.266 / 44.393 |
+| First shield failure | Fitted | 8.090 / 8.753 | 7.443 / 9.230 |
+| First death and aftermath | Fitted | 12.947 / 13.868 | 13.066 / 13.598 |
+| First wreck submission | Fitted | 9.030 / 13.868 | 9.840 / 12.076 |
+| First shield hit window | Egg | 8.627 / 11.032 | 25.276 / 38.524 |
+| First shield failure | Egg | 8.699 / 13.230 | 9.300 / 10.200 |
+| First death and aftermath | Egg | 15.579 / 22.908 | 12.418 / 20.152 |
+
+The first five fitted draw frames peaked at 8.254 ms across the three launches. The fitted window's 27.120 to 44.393 ms peaks began 783 to 972 ms after dispatch, after the fitted shield's glow expired. The egg also showed later peaks. At the longest fitted frame, the main process callbacks took 2.819 ms, render CPU took 2.139 ms and GPU took 2.281 ms. Pipeline counters stayed flat in all six shield-hit windows.
+
+Two controls skipped the first shield hit and kept the shield hidden through the same 2.3-second window. They still peaked at 40.783 and 22.952 ms. The intervals before the first process callback were 34.579 and 18.889 ms, respectively. The hit-enabled control peaked at 21.057 ms, with 17.848 ms before the first callback. These later gaps explain the over-20 ms samples in the shield-hit window. An aborted headless fixture check was still running during the first batch. It was closed before these controls, and the complete main batch is being repeated.
+
+### Scene 207 and dense storm on main
+
+Three fitted sessions per case, with 180 warm-up frames and at least 720 measured frames and eight seconds. Frame median and p99 are the medians across sessions. Worst is the longest individual frame. GPU median is the median of the session medians. Times are in ms.
+
+| Fixture | Resolution | Frame median | Frame p99 | Worst frame | GPU median |
+|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Scene 207 Max | 1080p | 8.329 | 16.166 | 58.463 | 2.508 |
+| Scene 207 Max | 4K | 7.444 | 18.001 | 50.535 | 5.576 |
+| Dense storm Max | 1080p | 2.395 | 4.424 | 6.780 | 1.695 |
+| Dense storm High | 1080p | 2.415 | 5.245 | 11.699 | 1.886 |
+| Dense storm Max | 4K | 5.802 | 7.642 | 17.741 | 5.208 |
+| Dense storm High | 4K | 7.147 | 8.642 | 9.305 | 6.732 |
+
+Scene 207 passed the 12.5 ms gate at both resolutions, using the 1080p frame median and 4K GPU median. Both resolutions exceeded Run 2's 50 ms worst-frame mark. The longest 1080p frame spent 50.938 ms in main process callbacks, with 2.768 ms on the GPU and no new pipeline builds. Its 4K counterpart spent 44.774 ms in main process callbacks, with 5.587 ms on the GPU.
+
+The storm comparison and baseline repeat are in progress. [Raw traces and session summaries](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/raw/run3/)

+const GAS_CARD_SUPPORT := """
+const float MIN_GAS_DENSITY = 0.002;
+// Leave room for rounding when an upper bound drops an empty fragment early.
+const float GAS_DENSITY_BOUND = MIN_GAS_DENSITY * 0.95;
+vec2 gas_band(float band) {
+	return band < 0.5 ? vec2(-4.0, 2.0) : (band < 1.5 ? vec2(1.0, 8.0) : (band < 2.5 ? vec2(6.0, 14.0) : vec2(12.0, 18.0)));
+}
+float gas_layer(float band, float y) {
+	vec2 limits = gas_band(band);
+	return smoothstep(limits.x, limits.x + 1.5, y) * (1.0 - smoothstep(limits.y - 1.5, limits.y, y));
+}
+vec2 gas_card_offset(inout vec2 vertex, vec4 card, vec4 centre, mat4 inv_view, float height_scale) {
+	float angle = card.y * 6.2831;
+	mat2 spin = mat2(vec2(cos(angle), sin(angle)), vec2(-sin(angle), cos(angle)));
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+	// The radial falloff fits inside a disc. Bound that disc by its nonzero
+	// height band in the billboard plane before rasterizing the quad.
+	vec2 up = vec2(inv_view[0].y, inv_view[1].y);
+	float height_per_unit = length(up);
+	if (height_per_unit > 0.0001) {
+		up /= height_per_unit;
+		vec2 across = vec2(up.y, -up.x);
+		float centre_y = (inv_view * centre).y;
+		vec2 limits = (gas_band(floor(card.w)) * height_scale - centre_y) / (height_per_unit * card.x);
+		// Add a small margin for rounding at the height edges. The fragment
+		// shader still applies the original radial and height fades.
+		limits = clamp(limits + vec2(-0.0001, 0.0001), -0.5, 0.5);
+		vec2 offset = across * vertex.x + up * mix(limits.x, limits.y, vertex.y + 0.5);
+		// The soft intersection uses Godot's interpolated VERTEX.z. Keep its
+		// original quad coordinate even though POSITION draws a clipped quad.
+		vertex = transpose(spin) * offset;
+		return offset;
+	}
+#endif
+	return spin * vertex;
+}
+"""

+# Issue 1070 performance evidence
+
+The [Run 2 report](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/README.md) has the original timings, raw traces and reproduction steps. [Battle comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_BATTLE.jpg) · [High and Max storm comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_STORM.jpg)
+
+## Run 3 cost baseline on main
+
+Main revision `0c41f332c956040112361444597d02be99a40b75` contains the content-keyed fitted shield cache from issue 1130. Run 3 uses the preserved Run 2 fleet. All 259 installed ship files matched the installed manifest, and both the ship and generated asset manifests matched Run 2. The replay probe follows main's scene-gate build signature and keeps Run 2's event sequence, sampling windows and three-minute load allowance. The first attempt hit main's one-minute timeout before sampling.
+
+The reference is for the flagship death (#1077), shield failure (#1078) and nebula wake (#1079). Use the same case, resolution, camera and timer when comparing a prototype. First-use results use 1080p Max and a fresh Godot process per session. The steady Scene 207 case uses 20 hulls and four launch wings, seeded volleys and the engagement camera. The dense storm case uses seed 4103, 31 storm hexes and 28 nebula hexes at radius 170. Its ships are idle and its weather runs live. The 4K cases render the 3D scene at 3840×2160 in the same 1920×1080 window.
+
+### Cold start at 1080p Max
+
+Each cell gives the median of the three session peaks and the worst frame across the three sessions, in ms. The first-hit row uses the full 2.3-second Run 2 window. The wreck row covers the submission frame and two frames on either side.
+
+| Event | Shield | Run 2 patched | Run 3 on main |
+|---|---|---:|---:|
+| First shield hit window | Fitted | 8.049 / 9.382 | 30.266 / 44.393 |
+| First shield failure | Fitted | 8.090 / 8.753 | 7.443 / 9.230 |
+| First death and aftermath | Fitted | 12.947 / 13.868 | 13.066 / 13.598 |
+| First wreck submission | Fitted | 9.030 / 13.868 | 9.840 / 12.076 |
+| First shield hit window | Egg | 8.627 / 11.032 | 25.276 / 38.524 |
+| First shield failure | Egg | 8.699 / 13.230 | 9.300 / 10.200 |
+| First death and aftermath | Egg | 15.579 / 22.908 | 12.418 / 20.152 |
+
+The first five fitted draw frames peaked at 8.254 ms across the three launches. The fitted window's 27.120 to 44.393 ms peaks began 783 to 972 ms after dispatch, after the fitted shield's glow expired. The egg also showed later peaks. At the longest fitted frame, the main process callbacks took 2.819 ms, render CPU took 2.139 ms and GPU took 2.281 ms. Pipeline counters stayed flat in all six shield-hit windows.
+
+Two controls skipped the first shield hit and kept the shield hidden through the same 2.3-second window. They still peaked at 40.783 and 22.952 ms. The intervals before the first process callback were 34.579 and 18.889 ms, respectively. The hit-enabled control peaked at 21.057 ms, with 17.848 ms before the first callback. These later gaps explain the over-20 ms samples in the shield-hit window. An aborted headless fixture check was still running during the first batch. It was closed before these controls, and the complete main batch is being repeated.
+
+### Scene 207 and dense storm on main
+
+Three fitted sessions per case, with 180 warm-up frames and at least 720 measured frames and eight seconds. Frame median and p99 are the medians across sessions. Worst is the longest individual frame. GPU median is the median of the session medians. Times are in ms.
+
+| Fixture | Resolution | Frame median | Frame p99 | Worst frame | GPU median |
+|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Scene 207 Max | 1080p | 8.329 | 16.166 | 58.463 | 2.508 |
+| Scene 207 Max | 4K | 7.444 | 18.001 | 50.535 | 5.576 |
+| Dense storm Max | 1080p | 2.395 | 4.424 | 6.780 | 1.695 |
+| Dense storm High | 1080p | 2.415 | 5.245 | 11.699 | 1.886 |
+| Dense storm Max | 4K | 5.802 | 7.642 | 17.741 | 5.208 |
+| Dense storm High | 4K | 7.147 | 8.642 | 9.305 | 6.732 |
+
+Scene 207 passed the 12.5 ms gate at both resolutions, using the 1080p frame median and 4K GPU median. Both resolutions exceeded Run 2's 50 ms worst-frame mark. The longest 1080p frame spent 50.938 ms in main process callbacks, with 2.768 ms on the GPU and no new pipeline builds. Its 4K counterpart spent 44.774 ms in main process callbacks, with 5.587 ms on the GPU.
+
+The storm comparison and baseline repeat are in progress. [Raw traces and session summaries](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/raw/run3/)

+func _bake_gas_lattice() -> void:
+	const LATTICE_SIDE := 96
+	const ORIGIN := Vector3(-48, -32, -48)
+	var scale := _f32(float(SHADERS.HASH_SCALE))
+	var bias := Vector3.ONE * float(SHADERS.HASH_BIAS)
+	var volume = load("res://world/nebula_noise_data.gd").new()
+	volume.side = LATTICE_SIDE
+	volume.origin = ORIGIN
+	for z in LATTICE_SIDE:
+		var bytes := PackedByteArray()
+		bytes.resize(LATTICE_SIDE * LATTICE_SIDE * 4)
+		for y in LATTICE_SIDE:
+			for x in LATTICE_SIDE:
+				var p := (ORIGIN + Vector3(x, y, z)) * scale
+				p -= p.floor()
+				var q := Vector3(p.z, p.y, p.x) + bias
+				# Round each step to shader precision, fusing multiply and add.
+				var offset := _f32(p.z * q.z)
+				offset = _f32(p.y * q.y + offset)
+				offset = _f32(p.x * q.x + offset)
+				p += Vector3.ONE * offset
+				var value := _f32(_f32(p.x + p.y) * p.z)
+				bytes.encode_float((y * LATTICE_SIDE + x) * 4, value - floorf(value))
+		volume.slices.append(Image.create_from_data(LATTICE_SIDE, LATTICE_SIDE, false, Image.FORMAT_RF, bytes))
+	var error := ResourceSaver.save(volume, "res://world/gas_hash_lattice.res", ResourceSaver.FLAG_COMPRESS)
+	print("GAS_HASH_LATTICE 96x96x96 RF result ", error)
+	quit(0 if error == OK else 1)
+
+
+func _f32(value: float) -> float:
+	return Vector2(value, 0.0).x

+const GAS_CARD_SUPPORT := """
+const float MIN_GAS_DENSITY = 0.002;
+// Leave room for rounding when an upper bound drops an empty fragment early.
+const float GAS_DENSITY_BOUND = MIN_GAS_DENSITY * 0.95;
+vec2 gas_band(float band) {
+	return band < 0.5 ? vec2(-4.0, 2.0) : (band < 1.5 ? vec2(1.0, 8.0) : (band < 2.5 ? vec2(6.0, 14.0) : vec2(12.0, 18.0)));
+}
+float gas_layer(float band, float y) {
+	vec2 limits = gas_band(band);
+	return smoothstep(limits.x, limits.x + 1.5, y) * (1.0 - smoothstep(limits.y - 1.5, limits.y, y));
+}
+vec2 gas_card_offset(inout vec2 vertex, vec4 card, vec4 centre, mat4 inv_view, float height_scale) {
+	float angle = card.y * 6.2831;
+	mat2 spin = mat2(vec2(cos(angle), sin(angle)), vec2(-sin(angle), cos(angle)));
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+	// The radial falloff fits inside a disc. Bound that disc by its nonzero
+	// height band in the billboard plane before rasterizing the quad.
+	vec2 up = vec2(inv_view[0].y, inv_view[1].y);
+	float height_per_unit = length(up);
+	if (height_per_unit > 0.0001) {
+		up /= height_per_unit;
+		vec2 across = vec2(up.y, -up.x);
+		float centre_y = (inv_view * centre).y;
+		vec2 limits = (gas_band(floor(card.w)) * height_scale - centre_y) / (height_per_unit * card.x);
+		// Add a small margin for rounding at the height edges. The fragment
+		// shader still applies the original radial and height fades.
+		limits = clamp(limits + vec2(-0.0001, 0.0001), -0.5, 0.5);
+		vec2 offset = across * vertex.x + up * mix(limits.x, limits.y, vertex.y + 0.5);
+		// The soft intersection uses Godot's interpolated VERTEX.z. Keep its
+		// original quad coordinate even though POSITION draws a clipped quad.
+		vertex = transpose(spin) * offset;
+		return offset;
+	}
+#endif
+	return spin * vertex;
+}
+"""

+# Issue 1070 performance evidence
+
+The [Run 2 report](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/README.md) has the original timings, raw traces and reproduction steps. [Battle comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_BATTLE.jpg) · [High and Max storm comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_STORM.jpg)
+
+## Run 3 cost baseline on main
+
+Main revision `0c41f332c956040112361444597d02be99a40b75` contains the content-keyed fitted shield cache from issue 1130. Run 3 uses the preserved Run 2 fleet. All 259 installed ship files matched the installed manifest, and both the ship and generated asset manifests matched Run 2. The replay probe follows main's scene-gate build signature and keeps Run 2's event sequence, sampling windows and three-minute load allowance. The first attempt hit main's one-minute timeout before sampling.
+
+The reference is for the flagship death (#1077), shield failure (#1078) and nebula wake (#1079). Use the same case, resolution, camera and timer when comparing a prototype. First-use results use 1080p Max and a fresh Godot process per session. The steady Scene 207 case uses 20 hulls and four launch wings, seeded volleys and the engagement camera. The dense storm case uses seed 4103, 31 storm hexes and 28 nebula hexes at radius 170. Its ships are idle and its weather runs live. The 4K cases render the 3D scene at 3840×2160 in the same 1920×1080 window.
+
+### Cold start at 1080p Max
+
+Each cell gives the median of the three session peaks and the worst frame across the three sessions, in ms. The first-hit row uses the full 2.3-second Run 2 window. The wreck row covers the submission frame and two frames on either side.
+
+| Event | Shield | Run 2 patched | Run 3 on main |
+|---|---|---:|---:|
+| First shield hit window | Fitted | 8.049 / 9.382 | 20.911 / 35.591 |
+| First shield failure | Fitted | 8.090 / 8.753 | 7.783 / 8.555 |
+| First death and aftermath | Fitted | 12.947 / 13.868 | 9.753 / 10.934 |
+| First wreck submission | Fitted | 9.030 / 13.868 | 6.109 / 8.693 |
+| First shield hit window | Egg | 8.627 / 11.032 | 22.097 / 39.150 |
+| First shield failure | Egg | 8.699 / 13.230 | 7.430 / 9.012 |
+| First death and aftermath | Egg | 15.579 / 22.908 | 10.509 / 16.104 |
+
+The first five fitted draw frames peaked at 5.458 ms across the three launches. The fitted window's 20.488 to 35.591 ms peaks began 589 to 946 ms after dispatch. The egg showed a similar pattern. At the longest fitted frame, the main process callbacks took 2.279 ms, render CPU took 1.391 ms and GPU took 2.289 ms. Pipeline counters stayed flat in all six shield-hit windows.
+
+Two controls skipped the first shield hit and kept the shield hidden through the same 2.3-second window. They still peaked at 40.783 and 22.952 ms. The intervals before the first process callback were 34.579 and 18.889 ms, respectively. The hit-enabled control peaked at 21.057 ms, with 17.848 ms before the first callback. These later gaps account for the over-20 ms control samples. An aborted headless fixture check remained open during the initial main batch. The baseline uses the repeat after the process was closed. The initial traces are retained for comparison.
+
+### Scene 207 and dense storm on main
+
+Three fitted sessions per case, with 180 warm-up frames and at least 720 measured frames and eight seconds. Frame median and p99 are the medians across sessions. Worst is the longest individual frame. GPU median is the median of the session medians. Times are in ms.
+
+| Fixture | Resolution | Frame median | Frame p99 | Worst frame | GPU median |
+|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Scene 207 Max | 1080p | 8.329 | 16.166 | 58.463 | 2.508 |
+| Scene 207 Max | 4K | 7.444 | 18.001 | 50.535 | 5.576 |
+| Dense storm Max | 1080p | 2.395 | 4.424 | 6.780 | 1.695 |
+| Dense storm High | 1080p | 2.415 | 5.245 | 11.699 | 1.886 |
+| Dense storm Max | 4K | 5.802 | 7.642 | 17.741 | 5.208 |
+| Dense storm High | 4K | 7.147 | 8.642 | 9.305 | 6.732 |
+
+Scene 207 passed the 12.5 ms gate at both resolutions, using the 1080p frame median and 4K GPU median. Both resolutions exceeded Run 2's 50 ms worst-frame mark. The longest 1080p frame spent 50.938 ms in main process callbacks, with 2.768 ms on the GPU and no new pipeline builds. Its 4K counterpart spent 44.774 ms in main process callbacks, with 5.587 ms on the GPU.
+
+The storm comparison and baseline repeat are in progress. [Raw traces and session summaries](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/raw/run3/)

+func _bake_gas_lattice() -> void:
+	const LATTICE_SIDE := 96
+	const ORIGIN := Vector3(-48, -32, -48)
+	var scale := _f32(float(SHADERS.HASH_SCALE))
+	var bias := Vector3.ONE * float(SHADERS.HASH_BIAS)
+	var volume = load("res://world/nebula_noise_data.gd").new()
+	volume.side = LATTICE_SIDE
+	volume.origin = ORIGIN
+	for z in LATTICE_SIDE:
+		var bytes := PackedByteArray()
+		bytes.resize(LATTICE_SIDE * LATTICE_SIDE * 4)
+		for y in LATTICE_SIDE:
+			for x in LATTICE_SIDE:
+				var p := (ORIGIN + Vector3(x, y, z)) * scale
+				p -= p.floor()
+				var q := Vector3(p.z, p.y, p.x) + bias
+				# Round each step to shader precision, fusing multiply and add.
+				var offset := _f32(p.z * q.z)
+				offset = _f32(p.y * q.y + offset)
+				offset = _f32(p.x * q.x + offset)
+				p += Vector3.ONE * offset
+				var value := _f32(_f32(p.x + p.y) * p.z)
+				bytes.encode_float((y * LATTICE_SIDE + x) * 4, value - floorf(value))
+		volume.slices.append(Image.create_from_data(LATTICE_SIDE, LATTICE_SIDE, false, Image.FORMAT_RF, bytes))
+	var error := ResourceSaver.save(volume, "res://world/gas_hash_lattice.res", ResourceSaver.FLAG_COMPRESS)
+	print("GAS_HASH_LATTICE 96x96x96 RF result ", error)
+	quit(0 if error == OK else 1)
+
+
+func _f32(value: float) -> float:
+	return Vector2(value, 0.0).x

+const GAS_CARD_SUPPORT := """
+const float MIN_GAS_DENSITY = 0.002;
+// Leave room for rounding when an upper bound drops an empty fragment early.
+const float GAS_DENSITY_BOUND = MIN_GAS_DENSITY * 0.95;
+vec2 gas_band(float band) {
+	return band < 0.5 ? vec2(-4.0, 2.0) : (band < 1.5 ? vec2(1.0, 8.0) : (band < 2.5 ? vec2(6.0, 14.0) : vec2(12.0, 18.0)));
+}
+float gas_layer(float band, float y) {
+	vec2 limits = gas_band(band);
+	return smoothstep(limits.x, limits.x + 1.5, y) * (1.0 - smoothstep(limits.y - 1.5, limits.y, y));
+}
+vec2 gas_card_offset(inout vec2 vertex, vec4 card, vec4 centre, mat4 inv_view, float height_scale) {
+	float angle = card.y * 6.2831;
+	mat2 spin = mat2(vec2(cos(angle), sin(angle)), vec2(-sin(angle), cos(angle)));
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+	// The radial falloff fits inside a disc. Bound that disc by its nonzero
+	// height band in the billboard plane before rasterizing the quad.
+	vec2 up = vec2(inv_view[0].y, inv_view[1].y);
+	float height_per_unit = length(up);
+	if (height_per_unit > 0.0001) {
+		up /= height_per_unit;
+		vec2 across = vec2(up.y, -up.x);
+		float centre_y = (inv_view * centre).y;
+		vec2 limits = (gas_band(floor(card.w)) * height_scale - centre_y) / (height_per_unit * card.x);
+		// Add a small margin for rounding at the height edges. The fragment
+		// shader still applies the original radial and height fades.
+		limits = clamp(limits + vec2(-0.0001, 0.0001), -0.5, 0.5);
+		vec2 offset = across * vertex.x + up * mix(limits.x, limits.y, vertex.y + 0.5);
+		// The soft intersection uses Godot's interpolated VERTEX.z. Keep its
+		// original quad coordinate even though POSITION draws a clipped quad.
+		vertex = transpose(spin) * offset;
+		return offset;
+	}
+#endif
+	return spin * vertex;
+}
+"""

+# Issue 1070 performance evidence
+
+The [Run 2 report](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/README.md) has the original timings, raw traces and reproduction steps. [Battle comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_BATTLE.jpg) · [High and Max storm comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_STORM.jpg)
+
+## Run 3 cost baseline on main
+
+Main revision `0c41f332c956040112361444597d02be99a40b75` contains the content-keyed fitted shield cache from issue 1130. Run 3 uses the preserved Run 2 fleet. All 259 installed ship files matched the installed manifest, and both the ship and generated asset manifests matched Run 2. The replay probe follows main's scene-gate build signature and keeps Run 2's event sequence, sampling windows and three-minute load allowance. The first attempt hit main's one-minute timeout before sampling.
+
+The reference is for the flagship death (#1077), shield failure (#1078) and nebula wake (#1079). Use the same case, resolution, camera and timer when comparing a prototype. First-use results use 1080p Max and a fresh Godot process per session. The steady Scene 207 case uses 20 hulls and four launch wings, seeded volleys and the engagement camera. The dense storm case uses seed 4103, 31 storm hexes and 28 nebula hexes at radius 170. Its ships are idle and its weather runs live. The 4K cases render the 3D scene at 3840×2160 in the same 1920×1080 window.
+
+### Cold start at 1080p Max
+
+Each cell gives the median of the three session peaks and the worst frame across the three sessions, in ms. The first-hit row uses the full 2.3-second Run 2 window. The wreck row covers the submission frame and two frames on either side.
+
+| Event | Shield | Run 2 patched | Run 3 on main |
+|---|---|---:|---:|
+| First shield hit window | Fitted | 8.049 / 9.382 | 20.911 / 35.591 |
+| First shield failure | Fitted | 8.090 / 8.753 | 7.783 / 8.555 |
+| First death and aftermath | Fitted | 12.947 / 13.868 | 9.753 / 10.934 |
+| First wreck submission | Fitted | 9.030 / 13.868 | 6.109 / 8.693 |
+| First shield hit window | Egg | 8.627 / 11.032 | 22.097 / 39.150 |
+| First shield failure | Egg | 8.699 / 13.230 | 7.430 / 9.012 |
+| First death and aftermath | Egg | 15.579 / 22.908 | 10.509 / 16.104 |
+
+The first five fitted draw frames peaked at 5.458 ms across the three launches. The fitted window's 20.488 to 35.591 ms peaks began 589 to 946 ms after dispatch. The egg showed a similar pattern. At the longest fitted frame, the main process callbacks took 2.279 ms, render CPU took 1.391 ms and GPU took 2.289 ms. Pipeline counters stayed flat in all six shield-hit windows.
+
+Two controls skipped the first shield hit and kept the shield hidden through the same 2.3-second window. They still peaked at 40.783 and 22.952 ms. The intervals before the first process callback were 34.579 and 18.889 ms, respectively. The hit-enabled control peaked at 21.057 ms, with 17.848 ms before the first callback. These later gaps account for the over-20 ms control samples. An aborted headless fixture check remained open during the initial main batch. The baseline uses the repeat after the process was closed. The initial traces are retained for comparison.
+
+### Scene 207 and dense storm on main
+
+Three fitted sessions per case, with 180 warm-up frames and at least 720 measured frames and eight seconds. Frame median and p99 are the medians across sessions. Worst is the longest individual frame. GPU median is the median of the session medians. Times are in ms.
+
+| Fixture | Resolution | Frame median | Frame p99 | Worst frame | GPU median |
+|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Scene 207 Max | 1080p | 8.329 | 16.166 | 58.463 | 2.508 |
+| Scene 207 Max | 4K | 7.444 | 18.001 | 50.535 | 5.576 |
+| Dense storm Max | 1080p | 2.395 | 4.424 | 6.780 | 1.695 |
+| Dense storm High | 1080p | 2.415 | 5.245 | 11.699 | 1.886 |
+| Dense storm Max | 4K | 5.802 | 7.642 | 17.741 | 5.208 |
+| Dense storm High | 4K | 7.147 | 8.642 | 9.305 | 6.732 |
+
+Scene 207 passed the 12.5 ms gate at both resolutions, using the 1080p frame median and 4K GPU median. Both resolutions exceeded Run 2's 50 ms worst-frame mark. The longest 1080p frame spent 50.938 ms in main process callbacks, with 2.768 ms on the GPU and no new pipeline builds. Its 4K counterpart spent 44.774 ms in main process callbacks, with 5.587 ms on the GPU.
+
+### High storm rendering
+
+High bounds each gas card to its existing height band before drawing and rejects fragments whose density cannot reach the original cutoff. It samples a 96³ table of the existing noise hash values at lattice corners, with the same eased interpolation. Samples beyond the table still use the original hash. The bake is reproducible with `godot --headless --path godot --script res://world/nebula_noise_bake.gd -- --gas-lattice`. The packaged asset matched the trial bake byte for byte.
+
+Final timing and comparison captures are in progress. [Raw traces and session summaries](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/raw/run3/)

+func _bake_gas_lattice() -> void:
+	const LATTICE_SIDE := 96
+	const ORIGIN := Vector3(-48, -32, -48)
+	var scale := _f32(float(SHADERS.HASH_SCALE))
+	var bias := Vector3.ONE * float(SHADERS.HASH_BIAS)
+	var volume = load("res://world/nebula_noise_data.gd").new()
+	volume.side = LATTICE_SIDE
+	volume.origin = ORIGIN
+	for z in LATTICE_SIDE:
+		var bytes := PackedByteArray()
+		bytes.resize(LATTICE_SIDE * LATTICE_SIDE * 4)
+		for y in LATTICE_SIDE:
+			for x in LATTICE_SIDE:
+				var p := (ORIGIN + Vector3(x, y, z)) * scale
+				p -= p.floor()
+				var q := Vector3(p.z, p.y, p.x) + bias
+				# Round each step to shader precision, fusing multiply and add.
+				var offset := _f32(p.z * q.z)
+				offset = _f32(p.y * q.y + offset)
+				offset = _f32(p.x * q.x + offset)
+				p += Vector3.ONE * offset
+				var value := _f32(_f32(p.x + p.y) * p.z)
+				bytes.encode_float((y * LATTICE_SIDE + x) * 4, value - floorf(value))
+		volume.slices.append(Image.create_from_data(LATTICE_SIDE, LATTICE_SIDE, false, Image.FORMAT_RF, bytes))
+	var error := ResourceSaver.save(volume, "res://world/gas_hash_lattice.res", ResourceSaver.FLAG_COMPRESS)
+	print("GAS_HASH_LATTICE 96x96x96 RF result ", error)
+	quit(0 if error == OK else 1)
+
+
+func _f32(value: float) -> float:
+	return Vector2(value, 0.0).x

+const GAS_CARD_SUPPORT := """
+const float MIN_GAS_DENSITY = 0.002;
+// Leave room for rounding when an upper bound drops an empty fragment early.
+const float GAS_DENSITY_BOUND = MIN_GAS_DENSITY * 0.95;
+vec2 gas_band(float band) {
+	return band < 0.5 ? vec2(-4.0, 2.0) : (band < 1.5 ? vec2(1.0, 8.0) : (band < 2.5 ? vec2(6.0, 14.0) : vec2(12.0, 18.0)));
+}
+float gas_layer(float band, float y) {
+	vec2 limits = gas_band(band);
+	return smoothstep(limits.x, limits.x + 1.5, y) * (1.0 - smoothstep(limits.y - 1.5, limits.y, y));
+}
+vec2 gas_card_offset(inout vec2 vertex, vec4 card, vec4 centre, mat4 inv_view, float height_scale) {
+	float angle = card.y * 6.2831;
+	mat2 spin = mat2(vec2(cos(angle), sin(angle)), vec2(-sin(angle), cos(angle)));
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+	// The radial falloff fits inside a disc. Bound that disc by its nonzero
+	// height band in the billboard plane before rasterizing the quad.
+	vec2 up = vec2(inv_view[0].y, inv_view[1].y);
+	float height_per_unit = length(up);
+	if (height_per_unit > 0.0001) {
+		up /= height_per_unit;
+		vec2 across = vec2(up.y, -up.x);
+		float centre_y = (inv_view * centre).y;
+		vec2 limits = (gas_band(floor(card.w)) * height_scale - centre_y) / (height_per_unit * card.x);
+		// Add a small margin for rounding at the height edges. The fragment
+		// shader still applies the original radial and height fades.
+		limits = clamp(limits + vec2(-0.0001, 0.0001), -0.5, 0.5);
+		vec2 offset = across * vertex.x + up * mix(limits.x, limits.y, vertex.y + 0.5);
+		// The soft intersection uses Godot's interpolated VERTEX.z. Keep its
+		// original quad coordinate even though POSITION draws a clipped quad.
+		vertex = transpose(spin) * offset;
+		return offset;
+	}
+#endif
+	return spin * vertex;
+}
+"""

+# Issue 1070 performance evidence
+
+The [Run 2 report](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/README.md) has the original timings, raw traces and reproduction steps. [Battle comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_BATTLE.jpg) · [High and Max storm comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_STORM.jpg)
+
+## Run 3 cost baseline on main
+
+Main revision `0c41f332c956040112361444597d02be99a40b75` contains the content-keyed fitted shield cache from issue 1130. Run 3 uses the preserved Run 2 fleet. All 259 installed ship files matched the installed manifest, and both the ship and generated asset manifests matched Run 2. The replay probe follows main's scene-gate build signature and keeps Run 2's event sequence, sampling windows and three-minute load allowance. The first attempt hit main's one-minute timeout before sampling.
+
+The reference is for the flagship death (#1077), shield failure (#1078) and nebula wake (#1079). Use the same case, resolution, camera and timer when comparing a prototype. First-use results use 1080p Max and a fresh Godot process per session. The steady Scene 207 case uses 20 hulls and four launch wings, seeded volleys and the engagement camera. The dense storm case uses seed 4103, 31 storm hexes and 28 nebula hexes at radius 170. Its ships are idle and its weather runs live. The 4K cases render the 3D scene at 3840×2160 in the same 1920×1080 window.
+
+### Cold start at 1080p Max
+
+Each cell gives the median of the three session peaks and the worst frame across the three sessions, in ms. The first-hit row uses the full 2.3-second Run 2 window. The wreck row covers the submission frame and two frames on either side.
+
+| Event | Shield | Run 2 patched | Run 3 on main |
+|---|---|---:|---:|
+| First shield hit window | Fitted | 8.049 / 9.382 | 20.911 / 35.591 |
+| First shield failure | Fitted | 8.090 / 8.753 | 7.783 / 8.555 |
+| First death and aftermath | Fitted | 12.947 / 13.868 | 9.753 / 10.934 |
+| First wreck submission | Fitted | 9.030 / 13.868 | 6.109 / 8.693 |
+| First shield hit window | Egg | 8.627 / 11.032 | 22.097 / 39.150 |
+| First shield failure | Egg | 8.699 / 13.230 | 7.430 / 9.012 |
+| First death and aftermath | Egg | 15.579 / 22.908 | 10.509 / 16.104 |
+
+The first five fitted draw frames peaked at 5.458 ms across the three launches. The fitted window's 20.488 to 35.591 ms peaks began 589 to 946 ms after dispatch. The egg showed a similar pattern. At the longest fitted frame, the main process callbacks took 2.279 ms, render CPU took 1.391 ms and GPU took 2.289 ms. Pipeline counters stayed flat in all six shield-hit windows.
+
+Two controls skipped the first shield hit and kept the shield hidden through the same 2.3-second window. They still peaked at 40.783 and 22.952 ms. The intervals before the first process callback were 34.579 and 18.889 ms, respectively. The hit-enabled control peaked at 21.057 ms, with 17.848 ms before the first callback. These later gaps account for the over-20 ms control samples. An aborted headless fixture check remained open during the initial main batch. The baseline uses the repeat after the process was closed. The initial traces are retained for comparison.
+
+### Scene 207 and dense storm on main
+
+Three fitted sessions per case, with 180 warm-up frames and at least 720 measured frames and eight seconds. Frame median and p99 are the medians across sessions. Worst is the longest individual frame. GPU median is the median of the session medians. Times are in ms.
+
+| Fixture | Resolution | Frame median | Frame p99 | Worst frame | GPU median |
+|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Scene 207 Max | 1080p | 3.808 | 10.600 | 36.330 | 2.613 |
+| Scene 207 Max | 4K | 6.188 | 13.507 | 40.943 | 5.746 |
+| Dense storm Max | 1080p | 2.168 | 2.803 | 3.670 | 1.692 |
+| Dense storm High | 1080p | 2.395 | 2.621 | 13.156 | 1.905 |
+| Dense storm Max | 4K | 5.666 | 6.443 | 15.887 | 5.273 |
+| Dense storm High | 4K | 7.128 | 7.651 | 10.117 | 6.768 |
+
+Scene 207 passed the 12.5 ms gate at both resolutions, using the 1080p frame median and 4K GPU median. All six sessions stayed under Run 2's 50 ms worst-frame mark. The 1080p session medians were 8.409, 3.808 and 3.440 ms. The 4K GPU medians were 5.589, 5.758 and 5.746 ms.
+
+### High storm rendering
+
+High bounds each gas card to its existing height band before drawing and rejects fragments whose density cannot reach the original cutoff. It samples a 96³ table of the existing noise hash values at lattice corners, with the same eased interpolation. Samples beyond the table still use the original hash. The bake is reproducible with `godot --headless --path godot --script res://world/nebula_noise_bake.gd -- --gas-lattice`. The packaged asset matched the trial bake byte for byte.
+
+Final timing and comparison captures are in progress. [Raw traces and session summaries](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/raw/run3/)

+func _bake_gas_lattice() -> void:
+	const LATTICE_SIDE := 96
+	const ORIGIN := Vector3(-48, -32, -48)
+	var scale := _f32(float(SHADERS.HASH_SCALE))
+	var bias := Vector3.ONE * float(SHADERS.HASH_BIAS)
+	var volume = load("res://world/nebula_noise_data.gd").new()
+	volume.side = LATTICE_SIDE
+	volume.origin = ORIGIN
+	for z in LATTICE_SIDE:
+		var bytes := PackedByteArray()
+		bytes.resize(LATTICE_SIDE * LATTICE_SIDE * 4)
+		for y in LATTICE_SIDE:
+			for x in LATTICE_SIDE:
+				var p := (ORIGIN + Vector3(x, y, z)) * scale
+				p -= p.floor()
+				var q := Vector3(p.z, p.y, p.x) + bias
+				# Round each step to shader precision, fusing multiply and add.
+				var offset := _f32(p.z * q.z)
+				offset = _f32(p.y * q.y + offset)
+				offset = _f32(p.x * q.x + offset)
+				p += Vector3.ONE * offset
+				var value := _f32(_f32(p.x + p.y) * p.z)
+				bytes.encode_float((y * LATTICE_SIDE + x) * 4, value - floorf(value))
+		volume.slices.append(Image.create_from_data(LATTICE_SIDE, LATTICE_SIDE, false, Image.FORMAT_RF, bytes))
+	var error := ResourceSaver.save(volume, "res://world/gas_hash_lattice.res", ResourceSaver.FLAG_COMPRESS)
+	print("GAS_HASH_LATTICE 96x96x96 RF result ", error)
+	quit(0 if error == OK else 1)
+
+
+func _f32(value: float) -> float:
+	return Vector2(value, 0.0).x

+const GAS_CARD_SUPPORT := """
+const float MIN_GAS_DENSITY = 0.002;
+// Leave room for rounding when an upper bound drops an empty fragment early.
+const float GAS_DENSITY_BOUND = MIN_GAS_DENSITY * 0.95;
+vec2 gas_band(float band) {
+	return band < 0.5 ? vec2(-4.0, 2.0) : (band < 1.5 ? vec2(1.0, 8.0) : (band < 2.5 ? vec2(6.0, 14.0) : vec2(12.0, 18.0)));
+}
+float gas_layer(float band, float y) {
+	vec2 limits = gas_band(band);
+	return smoothstep(limits.x, limits.x + 1.5, y) * (1.0 - smoothstep(limits.y - 1.5, limits.y, y));
+}
+vec2 gas_card_offset(inout vec2 vertex, vec4 card, vec4 centre, mat4 inv_view, float height_scale) {
+	float angle = card.y * 6.2831;
+	mat2 spin = mat2(vec2(cos(angle), sin(angle)), vec2(-sin(angle), cos(angle)));
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+	// The radial falloff fits inside a disc. Bound that disc by its nonzero
+	// height band in the billboard plane before rasterizing the quad.
+	vec2 up = vec2(inv_view[0].y, inv_view[1].y);
+	float height_per_unit = length(up);
+	if (height_per_unit > 0.0001) {
+		up /= height_per_unit;
+		vec2 across = vec2(up.y, -up.x);
+		float centre_y = (inv_view * centre).y;
+		vec2 limits = (gas_band(floor(card.w)) * height_scale - centre_y) / (height_per_unit * card.x);
+		// Add a small margin for rounding at the height edges. The fragment
+		// shader still applies the original radial and height fades.
+		limits = clamp(limits + vec2(-0.0001, 0.0001), -0.5, 0.5);
+		vec2 offset = across * vertex.x + up * mix(limits.x, limits.y, vertex.y + 0.5);
+		// The soft intersection uses Godot's interpolated VERTEX.z. Keep its
+		// original quad coordinate even though POSITION draws a clipped quad.
+		vertex = transpose(spin) * offset;
+		return offset;
+	}
+#endif
+	return spin * vertex;
+}
+"""

+# Issue 1070 performance evidence
+
+The [Run 2 report](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/README.md) has the original timings, raw traces and reproduction steps. [Battle comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_BATTLE.jpg) · [High and Max storm comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_STORM.jpg)
+
+## Run 3 cost baseline on main
+
+Main revision `0c41f332c956040112361444597d02be99a40b75` contains the content-keyed fitted shield cache from issue 1130. Run 3 uses the preserved Run 2 fleet. All 259 installed ship files matched the installed manifest, and both the ship and generated asset manifests matched Run 2. The replay probe follows main's scene-gate build signature and keeps Run 2's event sequence, sampling windows and three-minute load allowance. The first attempt hit main's one-minute timeout before sampling.
+
+The reference is for the flagship death (#1077), shield failure (#1078) and nebula wake (#1079). Use the same case, resolution, camera and timer when comparing a prototype. First-use results use 1080p Max and a fresh Godot process per session. The steady Scene 207 case uses 20 hulls and four launch wings, seeded volleys and the engagement camera. The dense storm case uses seed 4103, 31 storm hexes and 28 nebula hexes at radius 170. Its ships are idle and its weather runs live. The 4K cases render the 3D scene at 3840×2160 in the same 1920×1080 window.
+
+### Cold start at 1080p Max
+
+Each cell gives the median of the three session peaks and the worst frame across the three sessions, in ms. The first-hit row uses the full 2.3-second Run 2 window. The wreck row covers the submission frame and two frames on either side.
+
+| Event | Shield | Run 2 patched | Run 3 on main |
+|---|---|---:|---:|
+| First shield hit window | Fitted | 8.049 / 9.382 | 20.911 / 35.591 |
+| First shield failure | Fitted | 8.090 / 8.753 | 7.783 / 8.555 |
+| First death and aftermath | Fitted | 12.947 / 13.868 | 9.753 / 10.934 |
+| First wreck submission | Fitted | 9.030 / 13.868 | 6.109 / 8.693 |
+| First shield hit window | Egg | 8.627 / 11.032 | 22.097 / 39.150 |
+| First shield failure | Egg | 8.699 / 13.230 | 7.430 / 9.012 |
+| First death and aftermath | Egg | 15.579 / 22.908 | 10.509 / 16.104 |
+
+The first five fitted draw frames peaked at 5.458 ms across the three launches. The fitted window's 20.488 to 35.591 ms peaks began 589 to 946 ms after dispatch. The egg showed a similar pattern. At the longest fitted frame, the main process callbacks took 2.279 ms, render CPU took 1.391 ms and GPU took 2.289 ms. Pipeline counters stayed flat in all six shield-hit windows.
+
+Two controls skipped the first shield hit and kept the shield hidden through the same 2.3-second window. They still peaked at 40.783 and 22.952 ms. The intervals before the first process callback were 34.579 and 18.889 ms, respectively. The hit-enabled control peaked at 21.057 ms, with 17.848 ms before the first callback. These later gaps account for the over-20 ms control samples. An aborted headless fixture check remained open during the initial main batch. The baseline uses the repeat after the process was closed. The initial traces are retained for comparison.
+
+### Scene 207 and dense storm on main
+
+Three fitted sessions per case, with 180 warm-up frames and at least 720 measured frames and eight seconds. Frame median and p99 are the medians across sessions. Worst is the longest individual frame. GPU median is the median of the session medians. Times are in ms.
+
+| Fixture | Resolution | Frame median | Frame p99 | Worst frame | GPU median |
+|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Scene 207 Max | 1080p | 3.808 | 10.600 | 36.330 | 2.613 |
+| Scene 207 Max | 4K | 6.188 | 13.507 | 40.943 | 5.746 |
+| Dense storm Max | 1080p | 2.168 | 2.803 | 3.670 | 1.692 |
+| Dense storm High | 1080p | 2.395 | 2.621 | 13.156 | 1.905 |
+| Dense storm Max | 4K | 5.666 | 6.443 | 15.887 | 5.273 |
+| Dense storm High | 4K | 7.128 | 7.651 | 10.117 | 6.768 |
+
+Scene 207 passed the 12.5 ms gate at both resolutions, using the 1080p frame median and 4K GPU median. All six sessions stayed under Run 2's 50 ms worst-frame mark. The 1080p session medians were 8.409, 3.808 and 3.440 ms. The 4K GPU medians were 5.589, 5.758 and 5.746 ms.
+
+### High storm rendering
+
+High bounds each gas card to its existing height band before drawing and rejects fragments whose density cannot reach the original cutoff. It samples a 96³ table of the existing noise hash values at lattice corners, with the same eased interpolation. Samples beyond the table still use the original hash. The bake is reproducible with `godot --headless --path godot --script res://world/nebula_noise_bake.gd -- --gas-lattice`. The packaged asset matched the trial bake byte for byte.
+
+| Resolution | High GPU on main | High GPU after | Max GPU on the same build | High frame median after | Max frame median on the same build |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| 1080p | 1.905 | 1.277 | 1.689 | 1.910 | 2.195 |
+| 4K | 6.768 | 4.421 | 5.239 | 4.865 | 5.634 |
+
+High had the lower GPU median and frame median in every matched session at both resolutions. The 4K High GPU medians were 4.421, 4.421 and 4.376 ms. Trimming cards alone reached 5.55 ms at 4K and still cost more than Max.
+

+func _bake_gas_lattice() -> void:
+	const LATTICE_SIDE := 96
+	const ORIGIN := Vector3(-48, -32, -48)
+	var scale := _f32(float(SHADERS.HASH_SCALE))
+	var bias := Vector3.ONE * float(SHADERS.HASH_BIAS)
+	var volume = load("res://world/nebula_noise_data.gd").new()
+	volume.side = LATTICE_SIDE
+	volume.origin = ORIGIN
+	for z in LATTICE_SIDE:
+		var bytes := PackedByteArray()
+		bytes.resize(LATTICE_SIDE * LATTICE_SIDE * 4)
+		for y in LATTICE_SIDE:
+			for x in LATTICE_SIDE:
+				var p := (ORIGIN + Vector3(x, y, z)) * scale
+				p -= p.floor()
+				var q := Vector3(p.z, p.y, p.x) + bias
+				# Round each step to shader precision, fusing multiply and add.
+				var offset := _f32(p.z * q.z)
+				offset = _f32(p.y * q.y + offset)
+				offset = _f32(p.x * q.x + offset)
+				p += Vector3.ONE * offset
+				var value := _f32(_f32(p.x + p.y) * p.z)
+				bytes.encode_float((y * LATTICE_SIDE + x) * 4, value - floorf(value))
+		volume.slices.append(Image.create_from_data(LATTICE_SIDE, LATTICE_SIDE, false, Image.FORMAT_RF, bytes))
+	var error := ResourceSaver.save(volume, "res://world/gas_hash_lattice.res", ResourceSaver.FLAG_COMPRESS)
+	print("GAS_HASH_LATTICE 96x96x96 RF result ", error)
+	quit(0 if error == OK else 1)
+
+
+func _f32(value: float) -> float:
+	return Vector2(value, 0.0).x

+const GAS_CARD_SUPPORT := """
+const float MIN_GAS_DENSITY = 0.002;
+// Leave room for rounding when an upper bound drops an empty fragment early.
+const float GAS_DENSITY_BOUND = MIN_GAS_DENSITY * 0.95;
+vec2 gas_band(float band) {
+	return band < 0.5 ? vec2(-4.0, 2.0) : (band < 1.5 ? vec2(1.0, 8.0) : (band < 2.5 ? vec2(6.0, 14.0) : vec2(12.0, 18.0)));
+}
+float gas_layer(float band, float y) {
+	vec2 limits = gas_band(band);
+	return smoothstep(limits.x, limits.x + 1.5, y) * (1.0 - smoothstep(limits.y - 1.5, limits.y, y));
+}
+vec2 gas_card_offset(inout vec2 vertex, vec4 card, vec4 centre, mat4 inv_view, float height_scale) {
+	float angle = card.y * 6.2831;
+	mat2 spin = mat2(vec2(cos(angle), sin(angle)), vec2(-sin(angle), cos(angle)));
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+	// The radial falloff fits inside a disc. Bound that disc by its nonzero
+	// height band in the billboard plane before rasterizing the quad.
+	vec2 up = vec2(inv_view[0].y, inv_view[1].y);
+	float height_per_unit = length(up);
+	if (height_per_unit > 0.0001) {
+		up /= height_per_unit;
+		vec2 across = vec2(up.y, -up.x);
+		float centre_y = (inv_view * centre).y;
+		vec2 limits = (gas_band(floor(card.w)) * height_scale - centre_y) / (height_per_unit * card.x);
+		// Add a small margin for rounding at the height edges. The fragment
+		// shader still applies the original radial and height fades.
+		limits = clamp(limits + vec2(-0.0001, 0.0001), -0.5, 0.5);
+		vec2 offset = across * vertex.x + up * mix(limits.x, limits.y, vertex.y + 0.5);
+		// The soft intersection uses Godot's interpolated VERTEX.z. Keep its
+		// original quad coordinate even though POSITION draws a clipped quad.
+		vertex = transpose(spin) * offset;
+		return offset;
+	}
+#endif
+	return spin * vertex;
+}

+# Issue 1070 performance evidence
+
+The [Run 2 report](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/README.md) has the original timings, raw traces and reproduction steps. [Battle comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_BATTLE.jpg) · [High and Max storm comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_STORM.jpg)
+
+## Run 3 cost baseline on main
+
+Main revision `0c41f332c956040112361444597d02be99a40b75` contains the content-keyed fitted shield cache from issue 1130. Run 3 uses the preserved Run 2 fleet. All 259 installed ship files matched the installed manifest, and both the ship and generated asset manifests matched Run 2. The replay probe follows main's scene-gate build signature and keeps Run 2's event sequence, sampling windows and three-minute load allowance. The first attempt hit main's one-minute timeout before sampling.
+
+The reference is for the flagship death (#1077), shield failure (#1078) and nebula wake (#1079). Use the same case, resolution, camera and timer when comparing a prototype. First-use results use 1080p Max and a fresh Godot process per session. The steady Scene 207 case uses 20 hulls and four launch wings, seeded volleys and the engagement camera. The dense storm case uses seed 4103, 31 storm hexes and 28 nebula hexes at radius 170. Its ships are idle and its weather runs live. The 4K cases render the 3D scene at 3840×2160 in the same 1920×1080 window.
+
+### Cold start at 1080p Max
+
+Each cell gives the median of the three session peaks and the worst frame across the three sessions, in ms. The first-hit row uses the full 2.3-second Run 2 window. The wreck row covers the submission frame and two frames on either side.
+
+| Event | Shield | Run 2 patched | Run 3 on main |
+|---|---|---:|---:|
+| First shield hit window | Fitted | 8.049 / 9.382 | 20.911 / 35.591 |
+| First shield failure | Fitted | 8.090 / 8.753 | 7.783 / 8.555 |
+| First death and aftermath | Fitted | 12.947 / 13.868 | 9.753 / 10.934 |
+| First wreck submission | Fitted | 9.030 / 13.868 | 6.109 / 8.693 |
+| First shield hit window | Egg | 8.627 / 11.032 | 22.097 / 39.150 |
+| First shield failure | Egg | 8.699 / 13.230 | 7.430 / 9.012 |
+| First death and aftermath | Egg | 15.579 / 22.908 | 10.509 / 16.104 |
+
+The first five fitted draw frames peaked at 5.458 ms across the three launches. The fitted window's 20.488 to 35.591 ms peaks began 589 to 946 ms after dispatch. The egg showed a similar pattern. At the longest fitted frame, the main process callbacks took 2.279 ms, render CPU took 1.391 ms and GPU took 2.289 ms. Pipeline counters stayed flat in all six shield-hit windows.
+
+Two controls skipped the first shield hit and kept the shield hidden through the same 2.3-second window. They still peaked at 40.783 and 22.952 ms. The intervals before the first process callback were 34.579 and 18.889 ms, respectively. The hit-enabled control peaked at 21.057 ms, with 17.848 ms before the first callback. These later gaps account for the over-20 ms control samples. An aborted headless fixture check remained open during the initial main batch. The baseline uses the repeat after the process was closed. The initial traces are retained for comparison.
+
+### Scene 207 and dense storm on main
+
+Three fitted sessions per case, with 180 warm-up frames and at least 720 measured frames and eight seconds. Frame median and p99 are the medians across sessions. Worst is the longest individual frame. GPU median is the median of the session medians. Times are in ms.
+
+| Fixture | Resolution | Frame median | Frame p99 | Worst frame | GPU median |
+|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Scene 207 Max | 1080p | 3.808 | 10.600 | 36.330 | 2.613 |
+| Scene 207 Max | 4K | 6.188 | 13.507 | 40.943 | 5.746 |
+| Dense storm Max | 1080p | 2.168 | 2.803 | 3.670 | 1.692 |
+| Dense storm High | 1080p | 2.395 | 2.621 | 13.156 | 1.905 |
+| Dense storm Max | 4K | 5.666 | 6.443 | 15.887 | 5.273 |
+| Dense storm High | 4K | 7.128 | 7.651 | 10.117 | 6.768 |
+
+Scene 207 passed the 12.5 ms gate at both resolutions, using the 1080p frame median and 4K GPU median. All six sessions stayed under Run 2's 50 ms worst-frame mark. The 1080p session medians were 8.409, 3.808 and 3.440 ms. The 4K GPU medians were 5.589, 5.758 and 5.746 ms.
+
+### High storm rendering
+
+High bounds each gas card to its existing height band before drawing and rejects fragments whose density cannot reach the original cutoff. It samples a 96³ table of the existing noise hash values at lattice corners, with the same eased interpolation. Samples beyond the table still use the original hash. The bake is reproducible with `godot --headless --path godot --script res://world/nebula_noise_bake.gd -- --gas-lattice`. The packaged asset matched the trial bake byte for byte.
+
+| Resolution | High GPU on main | High GPU after | Max GPU on the same build | High frame median after | Max frame median on the same build |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| 1080p | 1.905 | 1.277 | 1.689 | 1.910 | 2.195 |
+| 4K | 6.768 | 4.421 | 5.239 | 4.865 | 5.634 |
+
+High had the lower GPU median in every matched session at both resolutions. Its frame median was lower across sessions at both resolutions. The 4K High GPU medians were 4.421, 4.421 and 4.376 ms. Trimming cards alone reached 5.55 ms at 4K and still cost more than Max.
+
+[Raw traces and session summaries](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/raw/run3/)

+func _bake_gas_lattice() -> void:
+	const LATTICE_SIDE := 96
+	const ORIGIN := Vector3(-48, -32, -48)
+	var scale := _f32(float(SHADERS.HASH_SCALE))
+	var bias := Vector3.ONE * float(SHADERS.HASH_BIAS)
+	var volume = load("res://world/nebula_noise_data.gd").new()
+	volume.side = LATTICE_SIDE
+	volume.origin = ORIGIN
+	for z in LATTICE_SIDE:
+		var bytes := PackedByteArray()
+		bytes.resize(LATTICE_SIDE * LATTICE_SIDE * 4)
+		for y in LATTICE_SIDE:
+			for x in LATTICE_SIDE:
+				var p := (ORIGIN + Vector3(x, y, z)) * scale
+				p -= p.floor()
+				var q := Vector3(p.z, p.y, p.x) + bias
+				# Round each step to shader precision, fusing multiply and add.
+				var offset := _f32(p.z * q.z)
+				offset = _f32(p.y * q.y + offset)
+				offset = _f32(p.x * q.x + offset)
+				p += Vector3.ONE * offset
+				var value := _f32(_f32(p.x + p.y) * p.z)
+				bytes.encode_float((y * LATTICE_SIDE + x) * 4, value - floorf(value))
+		volume.slices.append(Image.create_from_data(LATTICE_SIDE, LATTICE_SIDE, false, Image.FORMAT_RF, bytes))
+	var error := ResourceSaver.save(volume, "res://world/gas_hash_lattice.res", ResourceSaver.FLAG_COMPRESS)
+	print("GAS_HASH_LATTICE 96x96x96 RF result ", error)
+	quit(0 if error == OK else 1)
+
+
+func _f32(value: float) -> float:
+	return Vector2(value, 0.0).x

+const GAS_CARD_SUPPORT := """
+const float MIN_GAS_DENSITY = 0.002;
+// Leave room for rounding when an upper bound drops an empty fragment early.
+const float GAS_DENSITY_BOUND = MIN_GAS_DENSITY * 0.95;
+vec2 gas_band(float band) {
+	return band < 0.5 ? vec2(-4.0, 2.0) : (band < 1.5 ? vec2(1.0, 8.0) : (band < 2.5 ? vec2(6.0, 14.0) : vec2(12.0, 18.0)));
+}
+float gas_layer(float band, float y) {
+	vec2 limits = gas_band(band);
+	return smoothstep(limits.x, limits.x + 1.5, y) * (1.0 - smoothstep(limits.y - 1.5, limits.y, y));
+}
+vec2 gas_card_offset(inout vec2 vertex, vec4 card, vec4 centre, mat4 inv_view, float height_scale) {
+	float angle = card.y * 6.2831;
+	mat2 spin = mat2(vec2(cos(angle), sin(angle)), vec2(-sin(angle), cos(angle)));
+#ifdef HIGH_GAS_CARDS
+	// The radial falloff fits inside a disc. Bound that disc by its nonzero
+	// height band in the billboard plane before rasterizing the quad.
+	vec2 up = vec2(inv_view[0].y, inv_view[1].y);
+	float height_per_unit = length(up);
+	if (height_per_unit > 0.0001) {
+		up /= height_per_unit;
+		vec2 across = vec2(up.y, -up.x);
+		float centre_y = (inv_view * centre).y;
+		vec2 limits = (gas_band(floor(card.w)) * height_scale - centre_y) / (height_per_unit * card.x);
+		// Add a small margin for rounding at the height edges. The fragment
+		// shader still applies the original radial and height fades.
+		limits = clamp(limits + vec2(-0.0001, 0.0001), -0.5, 0.5);
+		vec2 offset = across * vertex.x + up * mix(limits.x, limits.y, vertex.y + 0.5);
+		// The soft intersection uses Godot's interpolated VERTEX.z. Keep its
+		// original quad coordinate even though POSITION draws a clipped quad.
+		vertex = transpose(spin) * offset;
+		return offset;
+	}
+#endif
+	return spin * vertex;
+}
+"""

+# Issue 1070 performance evidence
+
+The [Run 2 report](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/README.md) has the original timings, raw traces and reproduction steps. [Battle comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_BATTLE.jpg) · [High and Max storm comparison](PERF1070_RUN2_STORM.jpg)
+
+## Run 3 cost baseline on main
+
+Main revision `0c41f332c956040112361444597d02be99a40b75` contains the content-keyed fitted shield cache from issue 1130. Run 3 uses the preserved Run 2 fleet. All 259 installed ship files matched the installed manifest, and both the ship and generated asset manifests matched Run 2. The replay probe follows main's scene-gate build signature and keeps Run 2's event sequence, sampling windows and three-minute load allowance. The first attempt hit main's one-minute timeout before sampling.
+
+The reference is for the flagship death (#1077), shield failure (#1078) and nebula wake (#1079). Use the same case, resolution, camera and timer when comparing a prototype. First-use results use 1080p Max and a fresh Godot process per session. The steady Scene 207 case uses 20 hulls and four launch wings, seeded volleys and the engagement camera. The dense storm case uses seed 4103, 31 storm hexes and 28 nebula hexes at radius 170. Its ships are idle and its weather runs live. The 4K cases render the 3D scene at 3840×2160 in the same 1920×1080 window.
+
+### Cold start at 1080p Max
+
+Each cell gives the median of the three session peaks and the worst frame across the three sessions, in ms. The first-hit row uses the full 2.3-second Run 2 window. The wreck row covers the submission frame and two frames on either side.
+
+| Event | Shield | Run 2 patched | Run 3 on main |
+|---|---|---:|---:|
+| First shield hit window | Fitted | 8.049 / 9.382 | 20.911 / 35.591 |
+| First shield failure | Fitted | 8.090 / 8.753 | 7.783 / 8.555 |
+| First death and aftermath | Fitted | 12.947 / 13.868 | 9.753 / 10.934 |
+| First wreck submission | Fitted | 9.030 / 13.868 | 6.109 / 8.693 |
+| First shield hit window | Egg | 8.627 / 11.032 | 22.097 / 39.150 |
+| First shield failure | Egg | 8.699 / 13.230 | 7.430 / 9.012 |
+| First death and aftermath | Egg | 15.579 / 22.908 | 10.509 / 16.104 |
+
+The first five fitted draw frames peaked at 5.458 ms across the three launches. The fitted window's 20.488 to 35.591 ms peaks began 589 to 946 ms after dispatch. The egg showed a similar pattern. At the longest fitted frame, the main process callbacks took 2.279 ms, render CPU took 1.391 ms and GPU took 2.289 ms. Pipeline counters stayed flat in all six shield-hit windows.
+
+Two controls skipped the first shield hit and kept the shield hidden through the same 2.3-second window. They still peaked at 40.783 and 22.952 ms. The intervals before the first process callback were 34.579 and 18.889 ms, respectively. The hit-enabled control peaked at 21.057 ms, with 17.848 ms before the first callback. These later gaps account for the over-20 ms control samples. An aborted headless fixture check remained open during the initial main batch. The baseline uses the repeat after the process was closed. The initial traces are retained for comparison.
+
+### Scene 207 and dense storm on main
+
+Three fitted sessions per case, with 180 warm-up frames and at least 720 measured frames and eight seconds. Frame median and p99 are the medians across sessions. Worst is the longest individual frame. GPU median is the median of the session medians. Times are in ms.
+
+| Fixture | Resolution | Frame median | Frame p99 | Worst frame | GPU median |
+|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Scene 207 Max | 1080p | 3.808 | 10.600 | 36.330 | 2.613 |
+| Scene 207 Max | 4K | 6.188 | 13.507 | 40.943 | 5.746 |
+| Dense storm Max | 1080p | 2.168 | 2.803 | 3.670 | 1.692 |
+| Dense storm High | 1080p | 2.395 | 2.621 | 13.156 | 1.905 |
+| Dense storm Max | 4K | 5.666 | 6.443 | 15.887 | 5.273 |
+| Dense storm High | 4K | 7.128 | 7.651 | 10.117 | 6.768 |
+
+Scene 207 passed the 12.5 ms gate at both resolutions, using the 1080p frame median and 4K GPU median. All six sessions stayed under Run 2's 50 ms worst-frame mark. The 1080p session medians were 8.409, 3.808 and 3.440 ms. The 4K GPU medians were 5.589, 5.758 and 5.746 ms.
+
+### High storm rendering
+
+High bounds each gas card to its existing height band before drawing and rejects fragments whose density cannot reach the original cutoff. It samples a 96³ table of the existing noise hash values at lattice corners, with the same eased interpolation. Samples beyond the table still use the original hash. The bake is reproducible with `godot --headless --path godot --script res://world/nebula_noise_bake.gd -- --gas-lattice`. The packaged asset matched the trial bake byte for byte.
+
+| Resolution | High GPU on main | High GPU after | Max GPU on the same build | High frame median after | Max frame median on the same build |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| 1080p | 1.905 | 1.277 | 1.689 | 1.910 | 2.195 |
+| 4K | 6.768 | 4.421 | 5.239 | 4.865 | 5.634 |
+
+High had the lower GPU median in every matched session at both resolutions. Its frame median was lower across sessions at both resolutions. The 4K High GPU medians were 4.421, 4.421 and 4.376 ms. Trimming cards alone reached 5.55 ms at 4K and still cost more than Max.
+
+The second take from each source matched by eye at radii 170 and 26. The largest mean RGB channel difference was 0.125 of 255 at radius 170 and 0.645 of 255 at radius 26. The wider view also varies slightly between repeats. [PERF1070_RUN3_STORM](../../issue-1070-codex/PERF1070_RUN3_STORM.jpg) · [Pixel comparisons](../../../../contrib/codex/perf_1118/run2/raw/run3/look_differences.json)
+
+The replay uses Vulkan Forward+, Godot 4.7.2 and the RTX 5080, with vsync off and one solo watchdog claim per process. Reuse the Run 2 staging method and preserve both asset manifests when overlaying main. Use `run.ps1 -Phase cold` for the six fresh launches and `run.ps1 -Phase baseline -Shapes fitted` with the `gate:max:1:base`, `gate:max:2:base` and `dense:<tier>:<scale>:native_lod` cases above. For the High still pair, use `proof.ps1 -StormHighOnly` on each staged source and `sheets.py --storm-high-only` to compare the second takes.
